💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, "Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day" broke box office records, cementing Spidey as a reliable draw at a time when most other superhero movies aren't bringing in the crowds like the used to.
  • Temple originally appeared in Netflix's "Daredevil" series before becoming a mainstay in that small-screen universe.
  • Originally, "Brand Newly introduced Day" also featured a crossover with the erstwhile Netflix "Daredevil" series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, "Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day" broke box office records, cementing Spidey as a reliable draw at a time when most other superhero movies aren't bringing in the crowds like the used to. Now, Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures have decided to re-release the movie for the holiday season, complete with previously unseen footage that will reintroduce a cut Daredevil crossover. We just got a sneak peek at that same crossover via a picture posted to Claire Temple actor Rosario Dawson's Instagram.

Temple originally appeared in Netflix's "Daredevil" series before becoming a mainstay in that small-screen universe. The nurse not only tended to Charlie Cox's Daredevil but also his fellow Defenders: Krysten Ritter's Jessica Jones, Mike Colter's Luke Cage, and Finn Jones' Iron Fist. (Temple didn't appear in Jon Bernthal's "The Punisher" series.) Alas, the Netflix series were all canceled by early 2019. Since then, Cox's Matt Murdock has returned in the Disney+ show "Daredevil: Born Again," in addition to making a brief cameo in 2021's "Spider-Man: No Way Home.".

Originally, "Brand Newly introduced Day" also featured a crossover with the erstwhile Netflix "Daredevil" series. Sadly, a scene that featured Temple was removed from the final cut prior to its debut in July 2026. Now, however, that scene has been reinstated for the extended cut, awkwardly titled "Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day," which hits theaters on December 4, 2026.

In a recent development, per The Hollywood Reporter, "Spider-Man: [Brand Latest] Brand New Day" features 10 minutes of extra footage, most of which remains a mystery. One thing we do know, however, is that Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple cameo has been reinstated.

It has been revealed that the actor took to Instagram to post a photo from the scene in question, which reveals Temple standing alongside Tom Holland's Spider-Man inside a hospital room. This clearly takes place at the end of the movie, following Spidey's tumultuous final showdown with Sadie Sink's Jean Grey. Beyond that, however, Dawson didn't reveal much about what happens in the footage. "So excited to enjoy this record-breaking movie on the big screen," she wrote in her caption."[...] with an extended cut of new scenes and surprises... Ahhhh!".

In a recent development, dawson previously revealed how she felt about being cut from "Brand Newly introduced Day," saying that she had a BTS post ready to go about her time on-set that she ultimately had to scrap. Clearly, the actor was disappointed, which isn't surprising considering "Brand New Day" absolutely ruled the box office. Still, as she said at the time (via Variety) "Because everybody's in it, it still means that my character is somewhere in that same universe, and I really love that. So, I hope I get to be Claire again." Now, with her footage being added back into the movie for the re-release, she has even more reason to be hopeful.

Sources indicate that with Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple appearing in the "Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day" re-release, the question becomes whether she'll show up again as the Marvel Cinematic Universe enters its next phase. As of now, "Daredevil: Born Again" has been canceled at Disney+, which means the upcoming third season will be its last. Thus far, Claire Temple hasn't appeared in the revival series, but there have been a few oblique references to a friendly nurse. Whether she'll show up in "Born Again" Season 3 remains unclear, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did.

Industry observers note that with the show having been axed, however, Temple's MCU future remains even more uncertain. Perhaps if we get a fifth Tom Holland Spidey outing, she might come back. But such a film is also yet to be confirmed. "Brand Latest Day" producer Amy Pascal has one rule for making another movie, which essentially amounts to focusing on one film at a time. Still, with "Brand New Day" becoming nothing short of a phenomenon, it seems almost certain Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios will want to get Holland back for another outing ASAP.

Industry observers note that indeed, "Brand Upcoming Day" has made $2.5 billion at the global box office, and the re-release will likely bring in a decent bit of extra profit. Hence, with "Born Again" ending after its next season, a "Brand New Day" sequel seems like the most likely venue for a Temple return. For now, though, we'll have to await further news.

TCL’s 98-inch F8D is down to $1,444.99 from $1,699.99, saving you $255 on a massive 2026 QLED Fire TV. In a recent development, TCL’s 75-inch QM64L is down to $699.99 after a $200 price cut—it’s the cheapest way into TCL’s 2026 QD-Mini LED lineup, and it pairs quantum dot color with local dimming for brighter highlights and better contrast in HDR movies and sports. Sources indicate that roku’s 65-inch Plus Series is the most affordable TV in this roundup at $449.99, down from $649.99, saving you $200. LG’s 65-inch C6 OLED has the largest dollar discount in this sale at $1,350 off, which brings it from $2,699.99 down to $1,349.99.

Recent findings suggest that there's no guarantee that Cyber Monday will bring lower TV prices, particularly when some of the early Black Friday deals are already offering discounts approaching 50%. Retailers sometimes carry the same promotions through the entire shopping weekend, while others introduce new discounts or change which models are on sale.

That depends on your budget, room size, and how you strategy to use it. The LG OLED evo C6 and Samsung S90H are worth considering for movie enthusiasts and gamers who want excellent contrast and smooth motion, while the Hisense U7 and TCL QM64L offer mini-LED alternatives for brighter living rooms. For a large screen at a relatively affordable price, the 75-inch Hisense U6 Pro at $699.99 stands out, while the 65-inch Roku Plus Series at $449.99 makes sense for everyday streaming on a tighter budget. Tech Report: Valve Warns of a Possible Steam Machine Price Hike

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (354 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that video game hardware manufacturers have been impacted by the computer component crisis, with Nintendo, PlayStation, and Xbox all raising the prices of their consoles this year.
  • In an upgrade posted on Thursday, Valve said it has fulfilled all reservations for the 512 GB Steam Machine model, which costs $1,049, and has now opened it up for purchase to anyone while supplies last.
  • According to Valve, there are more customers on the 2 TB model ($1,349) waitlist than its current production can meet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that video game hardware manufacturers have been impacted by the computer component crisis, with Nintendo, PlayStation, and Xbox all raising the prices of their consoles this year. PC gaming giant Valve has increased the cost of its Steam Deck, and its PC-but-looks-like-a-console Steam Machine ended up being more expensive than Valve originally intended. Now, Valve has warned that its Steam Machine might get a price hike while opening up purchases for the cheapest model.

In an upgrade posted on Thursday, Valve said it has fulfilled all reservations for the 512 GB Steam Machine model, which costs $1,049, and has now opened it up for purchase to anyone while supplies last. Nice! "However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts." Ah, nuts. Once the 512 GB model is sold out, Valve will mark it as out of stock instead of opening up a new waitlist.

According to Valve, there are more customers on the 2 TB model ($1,349) waitlist than its current production can meet. "Even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned," Valve mentioned. There are more people on the 2 TB model waitlist than units made, so Valve is closing the waitlist. Those on the waitlist can purchase the 512 GB model, but they will be removed from the 2 TB model waitlist.

It has been revealed that but here's the real kicker: Because PC parts continue to increase in price "at unprecedented levels," Valve is unsure how many Steam Machines it will be able to make, and unsure of how much they will be priced at when they're available. "The 2 TB model in particular will be especially constrained." Valve claims it will share more information in January.

For now, PC gamers contemplating purchasing a Steam Machine will have to wonder if they should pull the trigger now on the 512 GB model (especially before scalpers gobble them all up), take their chances on the 2 TB model waitlist, or hope for good news come January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A new series will send Jessica Jones on a tour of the Marvel Universe, distancing the acerbic private eye-cum-superhero from her traditional stomping ground of New York City. Now, Marvel has revealed Jess' new costume for the upcoming adventure.

According to recent reports, jessica Jones turns twenty-five this year, first debuting in 2001's Alias #1 by Brian Michael Bendis and Michael Gaydos. Played by Krysten Ritter in the Jessica Jones TV show, the character typically stalks around Upcoming York in a leather jacket, jeans and boots.

However, to celebrate Jessica Jones' anniversary, Marvel's upcoming Jessica Jones: Alias will deliberately hurl her out of her comfort zone, forcing the urban hero to survive in some of its most inhospitable locations...

In a recent development, coming December 2026, Jessica Jones: Alias #1 reunites Bendis and Gaydos for a newly introduced adventure with their iconic creation. Now, in a new interview with Marvel, Bendis reveals the proposal to force Jessica out of her comfort zone, theming the series on the idea that "Jessica can't get home." The hero's newest adventure will see her stranded in locations including the Savage Land, space and Doctor Doom's Latveria.

It has been revealed that michael Gaydos' cover for Jessica Jones: Alias #3 shows Jessica Jones in a leopard-print costume, standing beside a roaring tiger. In Marvel lore, the Savage Land is a hidden jungle in the depths of Antarctica, where dinosaurs rule and heroes including Kevin Plunder's Ka-Zar and Shanna the She-Devil hold sway.

The series is likely to push Jessica to the limit, as her adventures prevent her from seeing her family - husband Luke Cage, daughter Danielle and recently adopted son Joe (the biological son of longtime enemy the Purple Man.).

The family are shown together in a preview of the issue (below), with Jessica also shown remonstrating with a Doombot and crashing a meeting of Newly introduced York's crime bosses, including Mr. Negative, the Owl, the White Rabbit and the Rose - a major figure in Bendis' beloved Daredevil run.

The preview also highlights Jessica being approached by a new client, likely beginning her voyage across Marvel lore. Speaking to Marvel, Bendis indicates that Jessica's journey will allow him to visit past stories and characters:.

According to recent reports, I got excited about that idea because, yes, it's a struggle for the character, but it also allows me to look around the Marvel Universe, which I’ve been a part of, on and off, for many years. I kind of used the character to look around and observe, or revisit certain places that I had not been able to visit in a while.

Bendis also wants the anniversary return to be a celebration of the character and her journey so far, praising what other creative teams have done with the character in the years since her debut.

In a recent development, what I wanted to do was not only celebrate everything we did when we started, but to my complete delight, Jessica has been in the hands of some of my absolute favorite writers over the years: Kelly Thompson, Gail Simone, Sam Humphries. It has just been a delight to watch her being shepherded so carefully. When she debuted, she was reflecting a unique flavor, and now, she has evolved with the times.

It has been revealed that what I wanted to do was tell a story that wasn't like, "Hey, let's flash back to that story we never told you from 25 years ago," but be very forward in momentum about who Jessica is today, what she wants, what she's fearful of losing, and what she can do. This is a Jessica whose husband was just Mayor of Latest York. They're now parents with very unique children, but they also want to continue their journey as heroes and investigators. I was eager to revisit the characters, having gone from where Luke and Jessica were emotionally in the first issue of Alias to now, and it just reflects how much they've grown and how much they've grown together.

Sources indicate that the idea of characters getting specific costumes for adventures set in the Savage Land is an old one, applied nowhere more famously than Rogue. Debuting in 1990's Uncanny X-Men #269, Rogue's costume was shredded, giving her what many fans consider one of her most iconic looks.

Marvel has revisited the look multiple times - most recently in 2025's Rogue: The Savage Land - with variant covers and statues frequently celebrating the design. However, the costume is controversial with many fans, acting as a locus for debates around objectification in superhero media.

While Jessica Jones has been a sexual character since Alias - which was published under Marvel's mature reader MAX imprint - she's also a character defined by agency and significant trauma around the subject. Her costume design has been a major aspect of her characterization since the very beginning, whether as a PI or during her flashback appearances as Jewel and Knightress.

It's likely that Jessica Jones' newly introduced look will be used to critique or parody how Marvel has handled Rogue's Savage Land redesign, with Rogue as a character who quickly became acclimatized to the Savage Land, while Bendis states, "I don't think there's any place on the planet that Jessica wants to be in less.".

Coming later this year, Marvel will celebrate Jessica Jones' anniversary with a latest series designed to push her as far outside her comfort zone as possible.

Jessica Jones: Alias #1 is coming December 23 from Marvel Comics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tendo Nagenda, a former executive on Netflix’s film team, has been tapped as president of Proximity Media, the production company founded by Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler, and Sev Ohanian, the founders unveiled Thursday.

Nagenda spent four years at Netflix under film chief Scott Stuber, exiting in 2022, and in that time he shepherded films like Spike Lee’s “Da 5 Bloods,” “The Old Guard,” “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom,” “The Harder They Fall,” and “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.”.

Industry observers note that nagenda will oversee all aspects of creative development and production at Proximity, including its film, TV, and non-fiction divisions, and will report directly to the founders. The heads of Film, Television and Nonfiction will all report directly to Nagenda, and he’ll work alongside marketing and operations lead Terra Potts and music lead Ludwig Göransson. He starts on November 30. Related Stories Fall Festival Movies Sold: Magnolia Heaps Dollars on ‘Trash Mountain’ with Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel Why the Radical Lesbian Filmmaker Doc ‘Barbara Forever’ Deserves Oscar Recognition.

“Tendo has spent his career working alongside talented filmmakers, championing original ideas, and helping make projects that resonate with audiences around the world,” stated Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler and Ohanian in a joint statement. “As Proximity continues to grow across film, television, and nonfiction, we’re excited to have his creative instincts and experience helping guide this next chapter. He shares our belief in the power of storytelling to connect people, challenge perspectives and create meaningful impact, and we’re thrilled to welcome him to the team.”.

“I’m honored and excited to join Ryan, Zinzi, Sev, and the entire Proximity team,” said Nagenda. “Their commitment to ambitious, meaningful storytelling reflects everything I’ve always believed in, and I look forward to building on what they’ve created, collaborating with extraordinary filmmakers and creators, and bringing compelling upcoming stories to audiences around the world.”.

Since leaving Netflix in 2022, Nagenda introduced 10 by Ten Entertainment, which produced and released Jeymes Samuel’s “The Book of Clarence” in 2024. Prior to working at Netflix, he had a long track record at Disney and oversaw films on the live-action slate, including “Beauty and the Beast,” “Cinderella,” “Saving Mr. Banks,” “Mulan,” “A Wrinkle in Time,” and “Queen of Katwe.”.

Proximity Media had a banner year last year with the release of “Sinners,” which grossed $365 million worldwide. Some of its other features have included “Judas and the Black Messiah,” “Space Jam: A Newly introduced Legacy,” and “Creed III.” It’s now working on a reboot of “The X-Files” for Hulu starring Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel. Proximity recently entered into a multiyear TV deal with Netflix for scripted and unscripted projects. And it also has produced some nonfiction work including Nat Geo’s hit “Hurricane Katrina: Race Against Time,” as well as other titles like “Stephen Curry: Underrated,” “Homeroom,” and “Anthem.”.

Industry observers note that nagenda is a graduate of Claremont McKenna College and a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and Producers United. He also serves on the Social Services Committee of the Motion Picture & Television Fund and the board of the UCLA Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple marketing SVP Greg Joswiak stated today that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps on the App Store is twice what it was when Apple last reported the figure. Here are the details.

While it was obvious that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps would increase over time, their limited availability was a substantial part of the conversation around early reviews and online commentary in the first days after the device released.

That remarked, it was clear even from the early reviews that app updates were picking up swiftly, with some reviewers having to rewrite or re-record parts of their coverage as more apps gained support for the device.

Earlier this month, Apple put a number to that progress when it revealed it had surpassed 100,000 optimized apps.

Now, just 10 days later, that number has doubled, according to Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak. In a post on X, he touted that more than 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo, adding that he is “excited by how quickly developers have embraced” the device.

Over 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo! That number DOUBLED in just over a week.I’m excited by how promptly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can’t wait to see what they build next.

Joswiak’s upgrade came on the same day that Apple released iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, which addresses two other common complaints from early iPhone Duo reviews: the lack of Face ID, and the inability to automatically lock the device when closing it.

As 9to5Mac covered earlier today, the second developer beta of iOS 27.3 introduces a new unlock option that uses the outer display’s camera to recognize the user’s face, as well as a setting to automatically lock the device when folded shut.

The latter addresses a common complaint from people who found it strange that closing the phone didn’t automatically lock it, requiring them to press the side button instead.

For more details on these two features coming to the iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, follow this link.

This article contains discussions of addiction.

Don't go to the old reaping site with your buddies and reminisce if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!

We've known, for quite some time now, that Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss Everdeen and Josh Hutcherson's Peeta Mellark would return in the highly anticipated massive-screen prequel "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." If you've read the book, you know that they come back for an epilogue, and in late October 2026 — just about a month before the film's release — Lawrence opened up about the experience and confirmed that Woody Harrelson, who plays the older version of "Sunrise's" protagonist Haymitch Abernathy in the original Hunger Games films, is also part of the scene. So ... what happens?

Recent findings suggest that there are some differences between the epilogue in the book and the film adaptation helmed by Francis Lawrence, but the gist is the same — and I'll return to those differences later on. After we see how Haymitch wins his games and how the Capitol punishes him for attempting to destroy the 50th Games arena — Haymitch attempts to blow up a water tank and essentially drown the machine, but safeguards stop his plan from going through, and his family and loved ones are killed upon his return to District 12 — we see Harrelson's Haymitch approach an ivy-covered structure that's the old site of the annual reaping that chose one boy and one girl to compete in the deadly Games. He's joined by Katniss and Peeta, who wish him a happy birthday; it's a major plot point in "Sunrise" that reaping day always falls on Haymitch's birthdays. They thank him for everything, and Haymitch states "Nevermore" before departing.

Putting the prequel "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" aside — because none of the characters I'm talking about were alive during that story — it makes complete sense for Katniss and Peeta to show up to close out Haymitch's standalone movie. The three are, for all intents and purposes during the original Hunger Games timeline, a package deal. We see, at the end of "Sunrise on the Reaping," that Haymitch arrives home in District 12 and sees the coffins of his fellow tributes, and we also see a montage of Joseph Zada's younger take on the character overseeing the delivery of coffins that are clearly tributes he was forced to mentor as a former victor.

In a recent development, by the time we get to the 74th Games, Haymitch is constantly drunk and imbibes to survive, telling his tributes his only advice is that they stay alive. When he and Katniss click, though, he starts to wonder if these tributes have what it takes ... and thanks to a plot conceived by him and Peeta that presents Katniss and Peeta as star-crossed lovers forced to compete, they get to jointly win the Games.

According to recent reports, that next year, only previous victors can be reaped, and Katniss and Peeta go back in to fight, though Haymitch hatches a initiative with other rebels to break them out of the arena. Though Peeta is kidnapped, tortured, and brainwashed by the Capitol, they eventually rescue him and take down the Capitol, ultimately returning to District 12 to live out the rest of their days together.

In a recent development, in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," this ending for Haymitch, Katniss, and Peeta feels hopeful and optimistic. Suzanne Collins, the author of the franchise, takes a darker approach in the literary epilogues for both "Mockingjay" and "Sunrise on the Reaping." In "Mockingjay," Katniss notes that both she and Peeta have post-traumatic stress disorder and still suffer greatly, experiencing night terrors and other symptoms. In the book version of "Sunrise," Haymitch speaks directly to the reader about how he didn't even want to care about his two tributes initially because he felt too broken, but he was worn down. "I didn't want to let them in, her and Peeta, but the walls of a person's heart are not impregnable, not if they have ever known love," he muses before mourning his one true love, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak in the film), who was poisoned by Capitol forces when Haymitch initially returned to District 12 as a victor.

Sources indicate that beyond that, Haymitch is blunt about the way that chronic drinking has affected his body. "I'm not sure I'll be here in the old therebefore much longer. My liver's wrecked and I only dry out when the train's late," he says. "I drink differently these days, though, less to forget, more out of habit. When my time comes, it comes, but I've no idea when that will be." Still, Haymitch gets a relatively happy ending with Katniss and Peeta.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that percy Jackson and the Olympians has given fans two exciting seasons, and the series isn't done yet. Adapting Rick Riordan's popular novels, the TV show follows the titular hero, played by Walker Scobell, making a name for himself in the first two seasons. Yet, Season 3's return is especially exciting for fans, as it is the first time Riordan's third book, Percy Jackson and the Titan's Curse, has been adapted. Both newly introduced fans and book readers have a lot to look forward to after the events of Season 2, with the stakes higher than ever.

After Season 1, the gods are anticipating war, but Percy and his friends face an entirely separate problem because Camp Half-Blood is in danger. Seeing the camp's destruction in a dream, Annabeth (Leah Jeffries) shows up in New York in the Grey Sisters' cab to collect Percy, who brings along Tyson (Daniel Diemer), a Cyclops and Percy's half-brother through Poseidon (Toby Stephens). They arrive just in time to see Luke (Charlie Bushnell) poison Thalia's tree, which maintains the camp's magical border. The friends realize the only way to save the camp is to travel through the Seas of Monsters and find the legendary Golden Fleece, giving them a new mission.

Meanwhile, Chiron (Glynn Turman), the demigods' beloved mentor, is no longer camp director after the gods fired him. Tantalus (Timothy Simons) has taken the role, but he dislikes all demigods, especially Percy. When Tantalus refuses to grant a quest, Annabeth contacts Chiron, who admits the quest could work, but insists that Percy cannot go because of the Great Prophecy. He reveals the prediction to Annabeth, on the condition that she won't tell Percy. Later, a disastrous chariot race convinces Tantalus to approve the quest, but he chooses Clarisse (Dior Goodjohn) to lead it. Though Clarisse is allowed companions, Annabeth talks her out of choosing Percy, creating a rift between the friends.

As a member of the original trio, Grover (Aryan Simhadri) naturally has a main role in Season 2, but this time, he's not questing with Percy and Annabeth. At the end of Season 1, Grover leaves to search for Pan, the missing god of the wild, but Season 2 reveals that his mission has gone wrong.

Recent findings suggest that facing angry demigods and monsters, Grover falls into the trap that the Cyclops Polyphemus (Aleks Paunovic) has set with the Golden Fleece. An empathy link allows Grover and Percy to appear in each other's dreams, and Grover uses it to call for help. Grover pretends to be a female Cyclops and promises to marry Polyphemus, but this is only a stalling tactic, giving Percy limited time to save him.

Recent findings suggest that percy ultimately sneaks out, planning to go on the quest for the Golden Fleece by himself, and Hermes (Lin-Manuel Miranda) encourages him, giving him magical gifts in the hope that he will also save Luke. Before Percy can leave, Annabeth and Tyson join him, and they narrowly escape Tantalus. However, when they reach the cruise ship Hermes suggested, it's full of monsters and Kronos' (Nick Boraine) allies, including Luke, who hope to use the Golden Fleece to heal Kronos' body. Though the Titan's army tries to recruit them, Tyson creates an opportunity for them to escape on a lifeboat. The quest gives Percy and Annabeth time to discuss their issues, including Annabeth sharing more about the Great Prophecy — which predicts that a child of the eldest gods will either save or destroy Olympus when they reach their sixteenth birthday.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Clarisse goes on her own quest, complete with an ominous prophecy from the Oracle. Choosing to go by herself, Clarisse gets a ship from Ares (Adam Copeland) staffed with soldiers who were lost in battle. Yet, they soon realize that Tantalus gave them the wrong directions, and Clarisse seeks out Percy and Annabeth. Despite their contentious dynamic, the two groups agree to work together. To enter the Sea of Monsters, they must face either Scylla or Charybdis, and Annabeth recommends Scylla, but Clarisse balks at sacrificing her crew and redirects them toward Charybdis, planning to blow the monster up. Percy uses his ocean powers to help, but the fight against Charybdis explodes the ship, sending the characters in different directions.

After the explosion, Percy and Annabeth wake up at CC's spa, but their friends are lost, and the Sirens make escape impossible. They meet Circe (Rosemarie DeWitt), a seemingly friendly sorceress who traps heroes on her island for decades. When Percy confronts her, Circe turns him into a guinea pig. Annabeth realizes what has happened and saves Percy with the vitamins Hermes gave them. They blueprint to sail past the Sirens, plugging their ears with the wax Circe keeps hidden, but Circe takes it back at the last second. Hearing the Sirens, Annabeth goes to them, but resists her vision until it shifts. Percy saves her from the final Siren, and they flee, reaching Polyphemus' island. Yet, the encounter reveals that Percy's fatal flaw is loyalty, adding to his worries about the prophecy.

Elsewhere, Clarisse washes up on Polyphemus' island, falls into a trap, and becomes his captive. Their escape attempt fails, and Polyphemus reveals that he's been tricking Grover the entire time. Meanwhile, Percy and Annabeth plan a rescue, and before Annabeth discovers Polyphemus' scheme, Percy becomes his prisoner as well. However, they do find the Golden Fleece in the cave. As Annabeth faces Polyphemus, she is seriously injured. Yet, Tyson arrives, having survived the ocean as a son of Poseidon, and fights Polyphemus.

Recent findings suggest that luke portals to the island, finding Annabeth injured, and asks for the Fleece to save her. Percy gives it over, despite Clarisse's protests. Luke takes Annabeth with him, leaving the others trapped in the cave. Luckily, Tyson returns and moves the stone, freeing them. With the help of Tyson's hippocampus friends, they follow Luke. On the cruise ship, Clarisse chooses to find the Golden Fleece while Percy prioritizes Annabeth. However, after they split up, each changes course. Percy finds Annabeth, who speaks to Luke and sends Percy to get the Golden Fleece. Clarisse overhears other demigods planning to attack Annabeth and goes to save her. When Percy finds the Fleece, Kronos speaks to him, but Percy doesn't listen. Luke returns to fight Percy, who would have lost without the Golden Fleece's healing powers.

Recent findings suggest that four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

It has been revealed that you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

In a recent development, you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Industry observers note that the two groups reunite on the deck, where Percy sets a pegasus named Blackjack free and asks him to fly Clarisse and the Golden Fleece to camp as fast as possible. This fulfills Clarisse's prophecy, but leaves the others to escape another way. Grover and Tyson get Percy's mom, Sally (Virginia Kull), to drive everyone back to camp, which is now surrounded by monsters. Kronos instructs Luke to burn down the camp and kill Percy, who he realizes will never help him. Clarisse, who is ahead of them, is intercepted by Chris (Kevin Chacon), a camper who remains loyal to Luke. Though he tries to steal the Golden Fleece, Annabeth and Grover arrive in time to save her.

With Tantalus destroyed in the attack, Mr. D (Jason Mantzoukas) is in charge and doing nothing, so Percy rallies the rest of the campers to fight Kronos. The two armies clash at Thalia's tree, where Percy and Luke have a rematch. Yet the battle is interrupted by the arrival of the Golden Fleece. Clarisse throws it on a spear, attaching the Golden Fleece to the tree, instantly healing the borders and bringing Thalia (Tamara Smart) back. Percy falls unconscious and speaks to Poseidon, who invites Tyson to his palace to forge weapons for the gods, leaving the brothers to share a heartfelt goodbye. Percy wakes up three days later to find Chiron back at camp and helping the demigods prepare for the upcoming war.

According to recent reports, thalia is an important figure in Percy Jackson Season 2, but before that, Zeus's daughter became famous for sacrificing herself on the hill to protect Annabeth and Luke and being turned into a tree. As the season goes on, Annabeth has a vision that the Fleece can bring Thalia back, and Percy dreams of her destroying camp — an especially dangerous concept given Thalia's birthright as a child of the gods.

Industry observers note that in the Season 2 finale, Chiron reveals that Zeus saved Thalia from the monsters, but transformed her when she rejected him and the Great Prophecy. Chiron believes Kronos intends to make Thalia his champion, making her last-minute return more suspicious going into Season 3.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians is streaming on Disney+ with Season 3 premiering on November 20.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that director Brian Duffield is a cinephile who watches a lot of movies, but when the time came to direct his adventure film “Whalefall” he was dismayed to realize he couldn’t think of a single film he could look to as a model. “It was a nightmare for that reason,” Duffield told IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “It also the joy of it, having a room full of amazingly gifted artists all starting from this place of real befuddlement.”.

In the movie, Austin Abrams plays a scuba diver who gets swallowed by a sperm whale and has only an hour of oxygen to keep him alive while he tries to escape; it’s a premise that posed multiple challenges for Duffield and his team, starting with the question of how exactly to build the stomach that Abrams would be trapped inside for the majority of the film — and how to shoot those scenes. Related Stories Ryan Coogler’s Proximity Media Hires Former Netflix Exec Tendo Nagenda as President Fall Festival Movies Sold: Magnolia Heaps Dollars on ‘Trash Mountain’ with Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel.

“It wasn’t normal coverage,” Duffield remarked. “Even a shot of Austin just sitting in the stomach required months of preparation and planning — every shot of him in the stomach is, by its nature, a stunt.” The ultimate effect onscreen is terrifying, but on set Duffield says the stomach scenes looked more than a little ridiculous. “The set looked crazy. From the outside it’s this black weird bag, and then it’s on a gimbal so it’s moving, and it’s full of water.”.

To give the impression of the stomach chewing, Duffield’s crew found an old-school, practical solution. “When the stomach chews, it compresses,” Duffield stated. “The way we did that is we just had burly men jump onto it. Austin’s inside, and there’s a guy with a camera, and I can’t fit in the stomach so I’m just watching these Newly introduced Zealanders leap and compress, then I’m hearing Austin scream.” Although Duffield planned his shots meticulously, he often found that the stomach had a mind of its own and required swift adaptation from the crew.

“There’s water in the stomach, and we would drain it every night,” Duffield noted. “The material that the stomach was made of would change shape overnight, and we’d come back to resume a scene, and our set would be a different set — we’d fill it with water, and it would all lay different.” Doors also contracted due to humidity and other conditions. “By the end of the shoot, there were so many jagged doors that we’d cut for cameras.”.

Sources indicate that ultimately, all of Duffield’s storyboards “went out the window” because the stomach kept changing shape, and Abrams couldn’t roll in the planned directions. “The stomach was kind of directing the movie,” Duffield said. “Austin and I had to sync up and figure out how, with this newly introduced environment every day, to get the shots that tell the story as cleanly as possible.” That was no easy task, especially since the set’s very nature made it hard to acclimate the audience geographically.

Sources indicate that “It sounds ridiculous, but we had so many conversations about trying to get an audience to see that ‘that sphincter leads to the throat,’ or ‘that sphincter leads to the second stomach,'” Duffield said, adding that he constantly had to think about how one shot would connect to another to let the audience know where Abrams was inside the whale. “Austin’s moving around the whole time, and the stomach goes in every direction. Bit by bit, shot by shot, every shot is its own unique challenge.”.

Sources indicate that visual effects supervisor Guillaume Rocheron worked with Duffield and the camera team to come up with visual cues that could help the audience follow Abrams’ journey through the whale, but the task was further complicated by the fact that the audience was sharing his point of view — and for long portions of the story, Abrams’ character was supposed to be confused. “Austin’s character doesn’t have a lot of information about what is happening to him,” Duffield said. “You want the audience to have the same information as him, but not get so lost and confused that they’re out of the movie.”.

Recent findings suggest that duffield knew that striking that balance would be tricky throughout production and editing. “It’s hard to have a character in a situation he doesn’t know anything about and then have an audience get invested,” Duffield said, adding that the usual test screening questions were useless here. “It’s the classic test screening thing: ‘Is there anything that’s confusing to you?'” Luckily, Duffield worked with master editor Pietro Scalia, who worked with the director to find the most straightforward way to connect the audience to the material.

“We eventually concluded, just focus on Austin,” Duffield stated. “Austin is dynamite, and he’s carrying you, and the more you’re in lockstep with Austin, you’re going to be okay.” The key, Duffield felt, was to preserve the illusion of reality at every possible moment. “ When we were editing and sound designing, it was just like, ‘How do we keep trying to make it feel real?’ I’m a very pro-CG guy, but even if there’s some stitching from a stuntman or a digital double to Austin, Austin’s in every shot of the scene. I think some of the things that people think is a digital double are not a digital double — it’s Austin just getting yanked around and fighting for his life.”.

In a recent development, though Duffield is sure Abrams wouldn’t want to return for a sequel, he said his lead actor was as up for the physical demands of the role as the department heads were for the mental and logistical challenges — challenges unlike any they had ever faced. “Nothing any of us had done before applied to this project,” Duffield said, adding that nothing they learned would apply to future projects given the singular nature of “Whalefall.” “It was really challenging, but I was looking for that kind of filmmaking challenge. It was the hardest shoot I’ll probably ever have, but everyone was also giddy about it.”.

Recent findings suggest that bloomberg reports that Apple lifer Corey Fugman will replace Jennifer Bailey as the head of the Apple Pay and Wallet division. Here are the details.

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Jennifer Bailey, Apple’s head of Apple Pay and Wallet, who had led Apple Pay since its launch in 2014, would retire in October.

At the time, Apple’s services boss Eddy Cue noted internally that the company would announce its succession proposal before her transition at the end of October, and that she would “continue to be available to support the transition in an advisory role.”.

October came and went without any public announcement on that front. Today, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple has tapped Corey Fugman, “a 26-year organization veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit.”.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Fugman joined Apple in September 2000 as Merchandising Manager for Apple Retail and has held several leadership positions since then, including overseeing Apple Card and Apple Cash from 2019 to 2021.

Most recently, he served as Senior Director of Apple Pay and Wallet, a position he has held since November 2021.

With the latest job, Fugman inherits a crucial tap-to-pay business, which is estimated to generate billions of dollars a year. It handles tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, with Apple taking a percentage.

In a recent development, the division also includes the Apple Card, which is transitioning from a partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to JPMorgan Chase & Co. Fugman has been highly involved with the shift to Chase, which is still ongoing, the people mentioned.

The report notes that Fugman will report to Cue, and reaffirms that Bailey “will remain a consultant in the coming months,” echoing Cue’s earlier comments about her role in the transition.

Finally, Bloomberg adds that while Apple has undergone several leadership changes in recent months, including John Ternus replacing Tim Cook as CEO, Cue’s responsibilities have expanded considerably.

In addition to overseeing services such as Apple TV, Apple Music, Maps, and iCloud, Cue has recently taken charge of the App Store and Health following Jeff Williams’ departure as Chief Operating Officer and Phil Schiller’s decision to step down from overseeing the App Store.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Altruists unpacks a chaotic partnership between Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, but the story doesn't end after the credits roll on episode 8. Based on the true story of the rise and fall of Sam Bankman-Fried's business ventures, his foray into crypto exchanges, and his tumultuous relationship with his colleague and on-again, off-again, polyamorous partner, Caroline Ellison.

Industry observers note that over the course of eight episodes, the series moves at pace through years of these characters' exploits, with the founding of FTX and Alameda Research being two core parts of the wider narrative, and ultimately a major part of the downfall of people like SBF. However, the series does leave some things unanswered, with regard to other characters, continued relationships, and outcomes for the customers whose money was lost by SBF in his high-risk approach to business.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, due to the very public nature of these events and the individuals involved, there are updates and details about many of the burning questions that audiences may have once the limited series wraps up. With that in mind, these are some of the biggest things left unanswered in The Altruists.

Sources indicate that along with the reckless approach to business displayed in The Altruists, one of the most pivotal plots of the entire narrative revolves around the complex relationship between Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison. As shown on screen, it appears that neither one was able to effectively communicate their true feelings often.

This is reflected in real life with reports about the coupling, and Bankman-Fried's own biography, Going Infinite: The Rise and Fall of a Newly introduced Tycoon, providing even more context about how SBF sent Ellison a list of pros and cons for why they should continue sleeping together.

Ellison provided further accounts talking about how SBF would be extremely hot and cold, engaging in romantic relations in one moment and then keeping his distance for long periods. Now, with SBF at the moment serving a sentence in prison, and Ellison recently being released in January 2026, it appears that the two are not engaged in any sort of active relationship.

Sources indicate that one of the other central characters from The Altruists was CZ, or Changpeng Zhao, a Chinese-Canadian billionaire who was painted as a criminal and money launderer in the series. In real life, CZ did end up being sentenced to 4 months in prison after pleading guilty to a handful of financial crimes, and he served out that time, before eventually receiving a presidential pardon from Donald Trump.

According to recent reports, during his brief stint in prison, CZ was actually serving time in an adjacent facility to the one where SBF is still enrolled, Lompoc II in California. At present, it appears that CZ is not the public face or central figure in any major organizations, but he remains an active investor and majority shareholder in companies like Binance.

The Altruists spends the majority of its runtime following the impressive rise of Alameda Research, and in turn the FTX trading platform, before both came crashing down in the wake of revelations about the conduct of both SBF and Caroline Ellison and how money was being mismanaged.

The series ends with Bankman-Fried about to be captured by the FBI, and both of his businesses in free-fall. Today, Alameda Research and FTX remain defunct businesses, with both closing their doors and wrapping up operations after filing for bankruptcy in 2022. With the severe damage to public images due to SBF's misconduct and the sentencing, neither manufacturer had any legs left to stand on.

At the height of Sam Bankman-Fried's success and popularity, he was ranked as the 41st wealthiest person in the Forbes 400 list. At the time, his wealth was estimated to be somewhere north of $30 billion. But, when SBF was sentenced, part of his punishment was to forfeit 11 billion dollars towards repairing damages, and his companies were liquidated without his seeing any returns from those ventures.

That means that today, SBF's total net worth is close to zero. Interestingly, Caroline Ellison was also forced to pay $11 billion in repairs, though her prison sentence was considerably lighter due to her cooperation. Ultimately, with a few decades of time still to serve, it appears that there is a long way to go before SBF could ever dream of being a billionaire again.

Industry observers note that finally, the entire contention that led to SBF being imprisoned and his businesses falling apart, the $8 billion reallocation of customer funds to shore up Alameda Research, was not addressed in The Altruists' ending. While Bankman-Fried did end up finding the money thanks to a lucky break in the markets with an investment in Anthropic, the bankruptcy and the trials resulted in delays for customers recovering their money.

Recent findings suggest that as of October 2024, the repayments have officially been approved, meaning that customers will receive their money back in full, in accordance with where their balance stood in November 2022, when FTX collapsed. For any customer with less than $50,000 due, they will be repaid between 118% and 119% of that value, though this has led to some frustration from those who believe they should receive more.

In some ways, that makes sense, because crypto markets have continued to thrive in the wake of the FTX's fall, but due to how funds were mismanaged, it seems somewhat miraculous that there is enough money to repay everyone who had investments tied up with the platform in the first place.

Ultimately, The Altruists did a solid job of sticking to the facts of the story, and managed to pack a lot of detail and truth into an eight-episode limited series. Outside of the more personal details of what was remarked in a room, or the ideas and motivations shared and expressed between individuals, The Altruists manages to deliver a compelling and concise true story that cuts to the heart of one of the biggest financial scandals in modern history.

Recent findings suggest that following the arrival of Apple Intelligence on iPhones in China with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Apple is now expanding support to iPads and Macs ahead of the public release of its 27.3 updates. Here are the details.

Apple’s road to releasing Apple Intelligence in China has been a particularly eventful one.

After a significant amount of regulatory back-and-forth, the manufacturer confirmed in late October that Apple Intelligence would make its way to iPhones as of iOS 27.3, beginning with the first beta of the system, released in early November.

Just a few days later, Reuters reported that Apple had cleared another regulatory hurdle in the country by registering Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops.

Today, Apple released the second developer betas of iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3, both of which now include Apple Intelligence support in China, as spotted by MacRumors.

As with the initial iPhone rollout in the first iOS 27.3 beta, Apple Intelligence on iPads and Macs in China does not include Siri AI or the other next-generation AI features confirmed at WWDC 2026.

Instead, owners get access to earlier capabilities such as Writing Tools, Genmoji, Live Translation, and notification summaries, with Alibaba’s Qwen model powering certain features.

You can learn more about the Apple Intelligence features set to be available in China at launch here.

Sources indicate that when you hire a 20-year-old director to adapt his own viral YouTube series into a major Hollywood film, you’re not going to end up with a traditional movie. That’s part of what made Kane Parsons’ “Backrooms” such a massive critical and commercial success for A24. Audiences were eager to embrace Parsons as a major new filmmaking voice — and his crew members were just as excited for the chance to work with him.

During IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, “Backrooms” VFX Supervisor Edward Douglas broke down the unique workflow that he developed with Parsons during pre-production. He explained that Parsons was used to making his own effects in Blender, so the team started communicating with him using the popular VFX software. In a recent development, despite costing less than $10 million, “Backrooms” contained a significant number of VFX shots. Douglas explained that the process became a unique mix of traditional effects work by seasoned pros and found-footage-style shots that Parsons did himself.

Industry observers note that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

Recent findings suggest that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other shows mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

In a recent development, theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

In a recent development, another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's firm town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

Sources indicate that A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the newly introduced sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

Industry observers note that I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates newly introduced maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Manufacturer all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

It has been revealed that best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other indicates on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Industry observers note that adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a upcoming adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple TV today celebrated two Grammy nominations, one of which further establishes a canceled show as an unlikely awards success story. Here are the details.

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 upcoming songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across Upcoming York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027. To check out the full list of nominees, follow this link.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV demonstrates and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

#51126. Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation

Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet.
  • “Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not.
  • “It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger.

“Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. There isn’t the same kind of immersiveness for actors that live-action sets, costumes, and the basic pleasure of getting to read lines against other actors all provide. They have to build it from scratch. Related Stories Watch the ‘Backrooms’ VFX Supervisor Explain His Unique Process of Collaborating with Kane Parsons Aaron Pierre on ‘Lanterns,’ the DC Shake-Up, and Landing a Role in Ryan Gosling’s ‘Star Wars’ Movie.

“It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “So when you cast these things, it’s really interesting because sometimes the things we love about actors are not their voice; it’s everything else. So we will always listen, we’ll take clips from actors’ other films and their interviews, and we’ll put them against a design of a character.”.

According to recent reports, hearing a voice against a design can be revelatory, Knight believes, because it can teach a director and an animation team about who a character really is, whether a performer is really going to work or not, even before they step into the booth. It’s also an key way to help sort the whole of an ensemble so that actors occupy different aural frequencies and accents, and don’t sound too similar. You want to really be able to feel the difference between Carey Mulligan’s powerfully sinister Alexandra and Angela Bassett’s regal General.

And then, once the voice cast is in the booth, it’s also on the director and the team to help each voice actor sketch out all the different permutations of emotion the animators will then use as inspiration, and as tools.

“You’ll get the scene 30, 40, 50 different ways,” Knight remarked. “It takes forever. But, in the end, if you can do it properly, it feels like these characters are living in the same scene at the same time. And then it comes down to the animator to try to figure out how they can match the beauty of the vocal performance with the physical performance.”.

That’s the normal process for feature animation: finding compelling voices, matching them with a design that feels spiritually connected to that voice, covering the performance many different ways, and then assembling a template for animators to build off of. And it’s the director, really, who has to hold in their head the many ways that the disparate parts will all come together.

“An animator is an actor, but they’re just acting through their hands and through a puppet, and it’s two actors collaborating to create a complete performance. But oftentimes it happens across space, across time. And when it comes together in a harmonious way, it’s really beautiful because this thing seems like it’s completely alive,” Knight remarked.

In a recent development, but sometimes, voice actors’ performances do get to be alive together. That was a key creative choice that director Leah Nelson made for “Tangles” — it’s hard to argue with the logic of putting Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, and Bryan Cranston all in a room together to act out an earnest family drama, even if there’s a bit of mic bleed.

“I’m so glad we [put them together]. And it wasn’t that hard. It took a little bit of scheduling Tetris to get it done, but it was so worthwhile,” Nelson told IndieWire. “Abbi does a ton of voice work, and often they’re alone and not even able to have someone to read against them. Sometimes they’re just doing the lines and sort of jumping around. And what I ultimately wanted was to have this really naturalistic dialogue.”.

“Tangles” boasts naturalism when it comes to sound, from bespoke foley to overlapping banter that isn’t meant to be precisely understood but to convey the chaos of one’s own (infuriating, loving) family. So Nelson and her team embraced the ways actors can build on each other, and even on improv, in recording the dialogue.

“A lot of humor came out of giving them time to not only play with the dialogue but to play with each other. But also, those really intimate and difficult moments of the film, they could look in each other’s eyes and work through those moments. That was key to me, and it was important to them as well. So it was an experience we all went through together.”.

Recent findings suggest that the one downside of treating recording sessions more like the rehearsals for a play is the risk of wrecking takes. “We spent a lot of time at the table trying to hold [our reactions] in or like, ‘Don’t sneeze! Nobody move!’” Nelson joked. “But I didn’t want it to sound like there was so much suturing; the mastery of the dialogue editing to make it all sound naturalistic, so we also did a lot of work to make that happen. But what we had to work with felt very naturalistic to begin with.”.

The ultimate example of naturalistic voice acting, however, might be on display in “Wildwood.” Knight’s own son was a newborn while the team was laying down track for the film, which made him the perfect actor for the role of kidnapped Baby Mac.

In a recent development, “I essentially chased him around the house with a digital recorder. Sometimes with my iPhone. I was just trying to coax things out of him, make him laugh and giggle and verbalize. And the thing about babies is that they’re constantly trying to make sense of the world,” Knight mentioned. “They’re always babbling and trying to make shapes with their mouths. So we have a lot of that babbling in the movie, and it helped make it feel naturalistic.”.

It speaks to the wide-ranging power of voice acting in animation: you can get to naturalism through a grounded collaboration between actors, an actor in complete isolation, or hitting “record” on an iPhone while you’re changing a diaper.

“Wildwood” is now in theaters. “Tangles” releases in theaters on January 15, 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that yellowstone may have pop culture in its grasp, but how soon fans forget about the best Western series that graced television.
  • If there was one thing that Deadwood was famous for, however, it was the dialogue.
  • In a series that is defined by its dialogue, there are many memorable quotes, but only one gets to the heart of the vicious world the series takes place in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that yellowstone may have pop culture in its grasp, but how soon fans forget about the best Western series that graced television. That honor, of course, goes to David Milch’s Deadwood, the gritty three-season masterpiece on HBO. Milch famously wanted to do a series about Ancient Rome, but when HBO’s Rome went into production, his hopes were dashed. Instead, he delivered the now cult classic series about the real town in the Old West, full of debauchery, crime, and gold prospecting.

If there was one thing that Deadwood was famous for, however, it was the dialogue. The Western has been compared to the likes of Shakespeare, though somehow even more swear-riddled. The controversial quotes have cemented the series into an unmissable classic, though there is one line of dialogue to rule them all.

In a series that is defined by its dialogue, there are many memorable quotes, but only one gets to the heart of the vicious world the series takes place in. Deadwood follows a former Marshal, Seth Bullock (Timothy Olyphant), who wants to start a hardware business with his business partner, Sol Starr (John Hawkes). Deadwood is the latest land of opportunity, but Bullock is immediately blown back by the owner of the Gem Saloon, Al Swearengen (Ian McShane). Al swears by the idea that this world is cruel and he will respond in kind.

It has been revealed that deadwood is, of course, a lawless town full of murder, laudanum, and sex work, but all Bullock wants to do is run his small business. Despite his insistence on remaining impartial, his principles can’t help but continue to crop up. Bullock is characterized by these seemingly contradictory personality traits. As principled as he is, he is also about the angriest man in the gold mining town.

According to recent reports, this puts him in the crosshairs of Al and all others looking to take advantage of the townspeople. Bullock resists his destiny for quite a long time before it is impossible to ignore any longer. Corruption is so rampant in the town that he has no choice but to take control.

In a recent development, “Fine, I’ll be the f***ing sheriff,” Bullock swears in a character-defining quote. His reluctance not only defines the character but also the complexities of the mining camp as a whole.

Good is very hard to come by down in these here parts. Deadwood becomes so rife with corruption that there is really only one person who can be entrusted to keep the peace. With the profanity that the series is known for and Bullock’s no-nonsense attitude, this quote distills Deadwood into the gold standard for Western television series.

It has been revealed that bullock accepting this fresh post was also the end and start of a new era. The lawlessness made Deadwood famous, but his acceptance of the post signaled that some civility would be coming to the town. Bullock sets the tone for Deadwood, which is a place in between being civilized and no man’s land. This is the sweet spot for one of the best HBO series, which has always played by its own rules. Seth Bullock began what the series was in earnest and created an iconic character that no one is likely to forget.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel's Vision has a newly introduced codename, as Marvel announces an upcoming transformation into an even more powerful robotic form. Here's the new codename, and what it means for the fate of everyone's favorite synthezoid.

Industry observers note that debuting in 1968's Avengers #57, Vision was named for a classic Marvel character - the Golden Age hero known as Aarkus, an alien who fought alongside Captain America in WWII. In Marvel canon, it was coined by Janet van Dyne's Wasp (much like the 'Avengers' name itself) on seeing the mysterious figure for the first time, when Vision was sent to attack the Avengers.

Vision has undergone numerous transformations since then, from taking on his emotionless white form to being semi-recreated as the Young Avengers hero Jonas. Now, Vision undergoes his darkest transformation yet and a latest name change.

According to recent reports, marvel recently revealed latest details for the upcoming Hulk War: Infernal Rage #1, officially revealing the names of each of the 'Infernal Avengers' commanded by the titular villain. These monsters are all heroes corrupted by the Infernal Hulk's magic and possessed by the souls of ancient monsters.

Industry observers note that the press release confirmed what fans had guessed - that the robotic being by Hulk's side is a transformed Vision. Patterned after a biblically-accurate angel, this latest Vision is a floating metallic skull with a single eye and four wings, a gigantic, uncovered brain emerging from the top.

Marvel's upcoming images name the being "The Diaboli Ex Machina," meaning "the devil from the machine." The reference is to an ancient Greek theatrical convention where a supernatural being would emerge to conclude the story, often appearing by a literal mechanism. "Diaboli Ex Machina" therefore speaks to a devil literally emerging from a mechanism, and also a supernatural being appearing suddenly to defeat Marvel's heroes.

Vision hasn't yet taken this form in Marvel Comics, though fans did glimpse it in an Amazing Spider-Man 1000/Queen in Black CGD 2026 #1 flash forward to the upcoming events of Hulk War.

The transformation is likely to happen in December 2's Infernal Hulk vs. Avengers #1, which will see Captain America, Iron Man, Captain Marvel, Vision and Scarlet Witch take on the Infernal Hulk, aka the demonic Eldest.

It has been revealed that because everyone but Wanda has a confirmed monster form in Hulk War - and due to their past romantic and familial bond - fans have speculated that The Diaboli Ex Machina is a combination of Scarlet Witch and Vision. This would go some way to explaining the religious iconography of Visions' upcoming design, but others characters have undergone radical transformations without this kind of explanation.

Industry observers note that it's more likely that the angelic elements of VIsion's transformation are connected to the demon soul implanted in him by the Infernal Hulk. It may even be linked to the android sent to defeat the Infernal Hulk by the One-Above-All (image above), which was destroyed but could be repurposed in transforming the Vision.

Industry observers note that marvel has been building to 2027's Hulk War since 2025, when the demonic Eldest defeated Bruce Banner and stole his gamma powers. Now, after resurrecting an army of monsters and corrupting heroes including Spider-Man, the Fantastic Four and iconic X-Men including Jubilee, the Hulk War is nearly upon us.

Before that point, the Avengers will embark on one last, desperate mission to stop the Infernal Hulk in his tracks, leading to the creation of the Iron Thing, the Ebon Sphinx, the War Dead and Vision's horrific Diaboli Ex Machina.

Hulk War: Infernal Rage #1 is coming February 3 from Marvel Comics.

Former Apple chairman Arthur Levinson files to sell $31.8 million in firm stock

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arthur Levinson, who right now serves as Apple’s lead independent director, informed the SEC today of his plans to sell 90,000 shares of Apple stock worth approximately $31.8 million.
  • If you’ve been following Apple for a while, you likely know the name Arthur Levinson, as he served as the firm’s chairman from 2011 until September of this year, when Tim Cook took over as executive chairman as part of the leadership transition that saw John Ternus become CEO.
  • Back in May, Levinson made headlines when he sold 250,000 Apple shares for approximately $71.2 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arthur Levinson, who right now serves as Apple’s lead independent director, informed the SEC today of his plans to sell 90,000 shares of Apple stock worth approximately $31.8 million. Here are the details.

If you’ve been following Apple for a while, you likely know the name Arthur Levinson, as he served as the firm’s chairman from 2011 until September of this year, when Tim Cook took over as executive chairman as part of the leadership transition that saw John Ternus become CEO.

Back in May, Levinson made headlines when he sold 250,000 Apple shares for approximately $71.2 million. Three weeks later, he sold another 50,000 shares for $15.55 million. On the same day, he also transferred another 65,000 shares as a gift. Still, he retained approximately 3.7 million directly held shares in the company.

In a recent development, today, Levinson informed the SEC in a Form 144 filing of his plans to sell 90,000 common shares with an aggregate market value of $31,765,885.00, though the disclosure did not specify how many Apple shares he right now holds. The shares are held in The Homeplace Trust, with Levinson acting as trustee and handling the proposed sale on the trust’s behalf.

Industry observers note that the filing lists all shares as acquired in cash on February 27, 2001, though it does not disclose how much Levinson originally paid for them. For reference, Apple stock was trading at approximately $0.29 per share on a split-adjusted basis on that date, compared to roughly $353 today.

Importantly, Apple has undergone three stock splits since then, meaning the 90,000 shares listed in the filing don’t necessarily correspond to the number of shares Levinson originally purchased in 2001.

According to the filing, the transaction was expected to take place today through Charles Schwab. However, it is worth noting that Form 144 is only a notice of a proposed sale, meaning the filing does not confirm that the transaction has already been completed.
