In a recent development, what it's about: "Ambulance" is worth a look if you're in the mood for a high-octane action thriller. The brothers hijack an ambulance carrying an injured police officer and an EMT (Eiza González), sparking a chaotic, high-speed chase through Los Angeles.

In a recent development, why you should watch it: Michael Bay knows how to deliver a chaotic action thriller, and "Ambulance" is a great example of that. The film is packed with spectacular car chases, explosive set pieces and plenty of intense moments, with Jake Gyllenhaal clearly having a blast in his wonderfully unhinged role. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Eiza González also make a strong central trio, adding plenty of personality to the increasingly chaotic story.

Industry observers note that watch "Ambulance" on Netflix until Nov. 23.

What it's about: Set during the 1972 Munich Olympics, "September 5" follows an American ABC Sports broadcasting team whose coverage takes an unexpected turn when Israeli athletes are taken hostage by terrorists. With the world watching, ambitious young producer Geoff Mason (John Magaro) finds himself leading the live news coverage alongside TV executive Roone Arledge (Peter Sarsgaard). As conflicting reports emerge and time runs out, the team faces difficult decisions with lives hanging in the balance.

Sources indicate that why you should watch it: "September 5" is a fantastic choice if you enjoy tense dramas built around real-life events. The newsroom setting gives the historical thriller a real sense of urgency, with John Magaro delivering a particularly strong performance as the story unfolds. I also loved the attention to detail in its recreation of 1970s broadcasting, while the brisk pacing keeps the tension high throughout. Fans of journalism dramas like "Spotlight" and "All the President's Men" should definitely add this one to their watchlist.

In a recent development, watch "September 5" on Prime Video until Nov. 24.

What it's about: Set in the tense 72 hours before D-Day, this historical war drama follows General Dwight D. Eisenhower (Brendan Fraser) and meteorologist James Stagg (Andrew Scott) as they face a potentially history-changing decision. With dangerous storms threatening the Allied invasion of Normandy, Stagg must convince military leaders that launching the operation could be disastrous. But delaying it risks giving German forces time to uncover their plans, putting millions of lives at stake.

Why you should watch it: "Pressure" is a really gripping watch, especially if you enjoy WWII dramas based on true events. Andrew Scott is excellent, and Brendan Fraser makes a strong impression as Eisenhower. It takes a different approach to the war, focusing on the difficult decisions behind the scenes rather than constant battlefield action. There's still plenty of tension to keep you hooked, and the strong performances make it well worth watching.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a turn of fate somehow sadder than Punch the Monkey’s isolation and crueler than the loss of Harambe, the Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday that the beloved, internet famous Nile hippopotamus, Fiona, has died at the age of 9.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a tribute Thursday. “We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are.”.

It has been revealed that last week, vets reported that Fiona swallowed a knit hat that was accidentally thrown into her enclosure. Several days after the incident, Fiona’s appetite declined and zookeepers started a variety of tests and 24-hour care, in the hopes that Fiona could pass the hat naturally. (Surgery is a rarely recommended suggestion for hippos due to its high risk.) But Fiona continued to decline, losing energy and fluids.

Sources indicate that “Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover,” Thursday’s statement added. “Please keep her keepers and everyone who tried to help her in your thoughts as they try to navigate and come to terms with this shocking news. They are also, understandably, asking for space at this time.”  Trending Stories John Mayer Transports Michael J. Fox Back to the Future With Chuck Berry Performance CMA Awards 2026: The Complete Winners List Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Hardy Sing for Brooks & Dunn at Ferocious 2026 CMA Tribute Stephen Wilson Jr. and Chris Stapleton Collab on ‘I’m a Song’ at 2026 CMA Awards.

Fiona made history when she was born in 2017 as the first hippo born at the Cincinnati Zoo in over 53 years. (She was named after the Shrek character, princess Fiona, for the unique shape and size of her ears). Her mother, Bibi, was 17 at the time and went into labor early, delivering Fiona six weeks premature. Fiona was only 29 pounds and could not stand or nurse on her own.

Industry observers note that keepers and staff at the Cincinnati Zoo began documenting her growth on social media, drawing in millions of well-wishers and international fans as they watched the wobbling baby hippo fight to live and then begin to thrive. Even when Fiona reached adulthood, she remained a beloved internet icon known for her strength and resilience through seemingly insurmountable odds. Fiona was a fighter — even until the end.

How to hide the new macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override.
  • If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar.
  • I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:.

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false.

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

The command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:.

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR.

In a recent development, restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future update.

When iOS 27.3 beta 2 debuted earlier this week, we detailed how the enhancement introduces AI usage limits for Siri AI and select other features.

It has been revealed that for AI features that depend on server-based models, each device running iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, or macOS 27.3 will have limited daily access to advanced AI features. These include complex Siri AI requests, Image Playground, certain Photos app editing tools, and more.

The only iCloud+ tier that doesn’t include higher limits is the $0.99/month plan.

Read more: Apple reveals how iCloud+ increases Siri AI and Apple Intelligence usage limits.

In the Shortcuts app, the ‘Use Model’ action lets you choose between a few different model options, including Cloud, Cloud Pro, On-Device, and ChatGPT.

People should at least have the 200 GB model. When I worked at The Apple Store (Did Retail and Corporate) I always recommended iCloud, and highlighted the backup feature. I can’t tell you the amount of people who lost or got their phones damaged / destroyed and lost precious photos, videos that they could never get back. Nearly all signed up.

I did offer alternatives like backing to your Mac or external SSD, but to have a proper backup safety system you need 1-2 backups at home and one off site (ie. friends house, storage facility, etc.) and you would have to be consistent with your backups and drop offs. Most people don’t have the time so they do iCloud, same as I.

I’m at 2 TB, probably going to 6 TB, cause I love taking photos and videos of special events.

In a recent development, similar to Apple’s other AI usage limits, your access to the Cloud Pro model in Shortcuts increases if you have a higher storage plan. Per this support document, the 200GB plan supports standard limits, the 2TB plan offers 5x access, followed by 10x on the 6TB plan and 20x on the 12TB plan.

iCloud+ already provided far more than just increased cloud storage, but with iOS 27.3 it’s set to be an asset for AI power users too.

iCloud+ is available as a standalone subscription or through the Apple One bundle, which also includes Apple TV, Apple Music, and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO shook up the AI market and US economy last week, but now via The Wall Street Journal Huang has spoken out publicly for the first time since stepping down, and he signals he’s ready to return as CEO if asked.

Today Robbie Whelan at The Wall Street Journal published Jensen Huang’s first public statement since departing Nvidia last week.

Industry observers note that “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang stated in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the organization, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

To be clear, I’m also willing to step in as CEO of Nvidia if asked. I’ve owned several generations of their graphics cards, so I have plenty of experience with their products. More importantly, this is probably my best chance of finally having enough cash to afford a Mac with 32GB of RAM.

The timing is likely no coincidence, as Nvidia is set to report its quarterly earnings later today.

Even though Huang technically resigned as CEO rather than being fired, it was clear that his ouster wasn’t exactly his choice. Thus, today’s statement is the former CEO formally putting it out into the world that he’s ready to return if asked.

Since Huang stepped down, President Trump publicly called on Apple’s Tim Cook to step in as Nvidia CEO. But it’s expected that a fresh CEO—assuming it’s not Huang—will take much longer for the company to find and Cook is unlikely to want the job.

According to recent reports, what do you make of Huang’s remarks today? Let us know in the comments.

There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage.
  • In a recent development, that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • In a recent development, but to skeptics of the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication challenges." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

In a recent development, that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

In a recent development, but to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering latest security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

According to recent reports, mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find newly introduced security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be said for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

Sources indicate that you might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's notable to understand that just about every firm that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

According to recent reports, barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as promptly as possible.

Sources indicate that the implications aren't specific to any one manufacturer, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

It has been revealed that of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside latest features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a upcoming alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the firm’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the organization’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:.

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

Industry observers note that the first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Consumers can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the firm’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for quickly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

Industry observers note that and speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow consumers to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for customers looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are latest organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

In a recent development, once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, users can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal judge said that he will issue a ruling “as soon as I can” as to whether the Kennedy Center can proceed with its blueprint to close the arts complex for two years for renovations, amid fears that President Donald Trump ultimately will move to demolish the 55-year-old arts complex.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal judge said that he will issue a ruling “as soon as I can” as to whether the Kennedy Center can proceed with its blueprint to close the arts complex for two years for renovations, amid fears that President Donald Trump ultimately will move to demolish the 55-year-old arts complex.

Sources indicate that U.S. District Court Judge Christopher Cooper issued an injunction earlier this year that barred the center from closing unless its board conducted a more thorough analysis of its impacts on programming and other operations. The judge also ordered that Trump’s name be removed from the complex, with a tarp now covering the front facade after crews removed the lettering to comply with the order. Related Stories Legal Grand Trump Accomplishment: POTUS Defeats NYT Move To Toss $15B 'Lucky Loser' Defamation Suit News CBS And Paramount+ To Air Next Kennedy Center Honors.

Sources indicate that the Justice Department, representing the center, is seeking to lift the injunction, arguing that the board vote in August and September to close the center sufficiently examined all of the options, citing a report from Delta Consulting Group. The report concluded that a two-year closure would be much less expensive than keeping the center open during construction, a process that would take four years. Watch on Deadline.

“The court contemplated the exact course of action the center took here,” William Jankowski, attorney for the DOJ, told the judge.

Recent findings suggest that an attorney for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), an ex officio board member of the center who is challenging the board’s actions, argued that, despite the third-party Delta analysis, the board still has not considered the impact of a closure on such things as fundraising and programming.

Nathaniel Zelinsky, Beatty’s attorney, noted that the board “keeps rubber stamping the same decision.” Trump, who is the board chairman, revealed the closure plan in February, but Beatty’s legal team has claimed that the decision was not motivated by the renovation, but to mask the embarrassment of a drop in revenue after Trump’s name was added to the center’s official moniker.

Zelinsky also pointed to another analysis conducted by real estate firm, which highlighted that a four-year renovation plan that kept the center open would be far less costly than the Delta analysis. He said that the board never were given the JLL report before their August vote, but Jankowski told the judge that it still led to the some conclusion in recommending a two-year closure.

Beatty’s legal team asked that judge that, should be modify his injunction, he appoint a monitor to oversee the center, amid concerns over compliance with court orders and the performing arts institution’s finances.

Recent findings suggest that the center itself has had scant major programming since July, and the sprawling main building has been off limits to the public since September. The center indicates that the closure is temporary due to safety concerns, after a portion of the indoor ceiling plaster collapsed following rainstorms, as well as concerns of deterioration of supports for exterior soffit panels.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the center is going ahead with its annual Kennedy Center Honors, but in an alternate venue: The Capitol One Arena. The event is scheduled to take place on Dec. 7 and air on CBS on Dec. 27. The center also intends to proceed with the Mark Twain Prize, an annual ceremony honoring comedians and humorists, next year, Jankowski told the judge.

Trump has stirred concerns over demolition of the center after he raised the prospect in social media posts. He also was photographed on Air Force One in September reviewing a poster board that featured the lettering, “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED.”.

While the DOJ attorney argued that Trump’s remarks are not relevant to whether to lift the injunction, the judge still expressed concerns. In September, he ordered that he be given at least a 30-day notice before any such drastic changes be made to the center.

Norm Eisen, who also is representing Beatty, told reporters that they were trying to prevent a scenario like what happened to the White House East Wing, which Trump ordered demolished last year to make room for a new ballroom, and the East Potomac Golf Course, where the National Park Service abruptly cut down hundreds of trees on a site that the president wants to remake into championship links.

“The most vital takeaway: There is no question in my mind that this judge, under any cirumstances, is going to allow the demolition of the Kennedy Center, just that East Wing or East Potomac Golf Course wrecking ball scenario,” Eisen mentioned.

After 13 years of buildup, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. The latest installment of the GTA franchise is unique in that gamers are playing both sides of Bonnie and Clyde style romance in Vice City. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos serve as the game’s main protagonists, with Lucia being the first playable female protagonist in the history of the franchise. Historically, GTA has represented culturally reprehensible instances of violence with what they say is a satire-heavy approach intended to exaggerate the criminal world they are depicting. Some of it — like killing prostitutes in order to steal their money in GTA III — has not aged as well as the rest of the franchise.

Sources indicate that this time things will feel a little different. Keeping up the romance between Jason and Lucia is a huge component of the gameplay. They are not only romantically involved but partners in a criminal enterprise; your decisions in relation to each other affect the gameplay. But for a certain selection of male gamers stuck in the GTA of their youth — in which beating strippers and hiring sex workers were some of the first viral video game content of the internet age — the notion that they might have to be nice to a collection of pixels arranged in a female form was a step too far.

“What is this cuck simulator” Youtube streamer Asmongold — who combines gaming coverage with right wing commentary for an audience of over two million — complained on Thursday He covered his hands with his face and writhed dramatically after being prompted by the game to take clothing and groceries for Lucia — who is about to be released from prison — out of the trunk of his car and into their apartment.

“She’s impulsive, stupid, jealous, she doesn’t understand her place in the relationship, she’s not skilled, she’s selfish, is emotionally manipulative,” so basically “there is no real redeeming quality about Lucia.”.

Some consumers have complained of an early game quest that prompts players to buy flowers for Lucia who — again — has just been released from prison.

GTA 6 is insanely cucked, half of the missions are jestermaxing and simping for girls.

Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free owners after requiring AI Pro in the past.

Google previously referred to this capability as a 24/7 personal agent before integrating directly into the main Gemini app experience in October. Above the prompt box on mobile (or below on the web), you’ll see “Chat” and “Task.” The first option is the existing chatbot, while the latter lets you “hand off even more tasks to Gemini.”.

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:.

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”.

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.”.

Powered by the newly introduced Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

Black Friday is an excellent time to score a newly introduced pair of headphones that would otherwise be a splurge, with retailers like Amazon and Walmart already offering massive discounts on tech essentials from top brands a week ahead of the holiday. One of the early Black Friday deals that should be on your radar is the Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2 headphones, a mid-range noise-canceling option that’s perfect for bass lovers and is at the moment 50% off, dropping to $119.99 (originally $239.99).

Sources indicate that powered by 40mm dynamic drivers, they offer reliable noise cancellation with the ANC slider set to max on the companion app, which lets owners adjust a range of controls and listening modes, including the intensity of bass. While brands like Bose will outperform in ANC quality, if you’re looking for noise-canceling audio gear that checks most boxes at a reasonable price point, the Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2 headphones are a smart choice, especially at over $100 off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Edward Burns’ micro-budget black-and-white family drama Beneath the Blue Suburban Skies debuted at the Toronto Film Festival in 2019.

Seven years later, the film is finally getting a release with a one-week awards-qualifying theatrical run in Upcoming York from December 25, ahead of a rollout in major cities in January.

The film stars Burns alongside Tony and BAFTA winner Jennifer Ehle with Hannah Dunne and Brian Wiles also among cast. Multi-hyphenate Burns is getting behind the film’s release via his production company Marlboro Road Gang Productions. The filmmakers are also getting behind Ehle who they view as giving an awards-worthy turn. Related Stories Casting Alex Hassell & Jennifer Ehle Join ITV Space Drama 'First Woman' Casting '1923': Jennifer Ehle Joins Taylor Sheridan's 'Yellowstone' Prequel.

Twenty five years after The Brothers McMullen made waves for Burns by winning the Grand Jury Prize at Sundance, the filmmaker returned in 2019 with another portrait of a working-class family. At the center of the film is Tina Collins (Ehle), who struggles with shame and anger toward her two adult children still living at home, and growing resentment toward her husband, Jim (Burns), whom she fears has held her back. As financial pressures mount, addiction and alcoholism further threaten the family’s fragile stability. Watch on Deadline.

Pic is produced by Burns (who also scripts and co-edited), Aaron Lubin and William Rexer (who also served as director of photography) for Marlboro Road Gang Productions.

In a recent development, there aren’t many notices for the film online. The few that can be found are positive. Variety’s review of the movie from 2019 praised the performances and Ehle in particular.

According to sources, the film did get distribution offers out of TIFF seven years ago but those didn’t chime with the producers in a tough releasing landscape for indie pictures. Then COVID hit. After finally being taken off the shelf by the team this year, the movie played at the Montclair, Austin, Ojai, Charleston and Seattle film festivals, and won Best Picture at the Boston and Richmond festivals. It screens next at the Key West Film Festival, where Burns will be awarded the Golden Key Award.

Sources indicate that the filmmakers are now gunning for Indie Spirit, Gotham, SAG, PGA, DGA, and even Academy consideration. Zero Dark Thirty and Lioness actress Ehle will be supporting Burns with press efforts in coming weeks.

Hollywood loves a comeback and it also loves a David vs Goliath story (even if awards season is tilted in favour of Goliath). Andrea Riseborough proved with her surprise nomination for To Leslie four years ago that it wasn’t impossible for very low-budget movies to break through.

It has been revealed that burns said of the film: “Having grown up a working-class kid on Long Island, I wanted to explore what I saw as a growing crisis facing working families today. With fewer well-paying entry-level jobs, a shortage of affordable housing, and rising drug and alcohol addiction, the promise of a better tomorrow seems to be slipping away. The American Dream—that your children would do better than you, and that you could take pride in their success as you reached middle age—was becoming increasingly elusive.”.

Burns is known for starring in movies including Steven Spielberg’s Saving Private Ryan, The Holiday and Man On A Ledge, while TV turns include TNT series Mob City and Public Morals. He has directed 16 movies, including The Brothers McMullen, She’s The One, and most recently Finnegan’s Foursome.

It has been revealed that ehle is a two-time Tony Award winner, for The Real Thing and The Coast of Utopia, and won a BAFTA for her role as Elizabeth Bennet in Pride and Prejudice. Her film work includes The King’s Speech, Zero Dark Thirty, Contagion and A Quiet Passion.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

My feelings were low-key hurt when one of my friends called me “The King of Gift Cards” last year after I passed them a wrapped-up box containing…you guessed it, a gift card!

I laughed at it, then went to the bathroom to look at myself in the mirror and say to myself, “I have to get better at my gift-giving next year.” Now that we’re near the closing stretch of 2026, I’m doing some super early Christmas gift planning. And this time, I’m veering away from my penchant for picking up a bunch of gift cards and throwing them at my friends and family like it’s a massive giveaway.

In particular, I’m going the extra mile to make sure I give my father something he truly cherishes. He doesn’t really ask for much around the holidays, but I still want to give him something extra special. Shopping for my mom is so much easier since she tells me exactly what she wants, but it’s a bit harder to do that for my dad.

With ChatGPT and Gemini in my corner, I used both chatbots to see which one could bring up the best gift recommendations. And one of them came out ahead a bit more than its competition.

Since I know my dad’s two main interests, I included them in my prompt alongside a few of his other faves to make sure both chatbots generated the most appropriate gifts possible. This is the prompt I ultimately went with:.

Recent findings suggest that “My father is a drummer and a vinyl collector. His favorite artists are Jimi Hendrix, James Brown, The Beatles, The Monkees, A Tribe Called Quest, and Prince. Show me the 7 best gift recommendations I should consider getting him for Christmas this year.”.

According to recent reports, chatGPT certainly understood the assignment, as it combed the internet and came back with a wide selection of books and records worth throwing onto my dad’s gift wishlist. As for items geared toward his profession and hobby as a drummer, the chatbot brought up one product that should be right up his alley. Alongside each of its picks, it attached them to different categories and listed their prices so I could have as much information about all its listed items as possible.

Here’s the full lineup of potential Christmas gifts that ChatGPT brought to my attention:.

According to recent reports, google’s chatbot responded to my prompt by listing an equally strong list of gifts that cater to my dad’s preferred artists and his love of drumming. Gemini produced some pretty descriptive summaries of each gift, just like ChatGPT. And as a helpful tip, it notified me that it’s worth thumbing through my dad’s vinyl collection and taking a picture of it so I don’t end up buying any duplicates.

This is the full list of gift recommendations Gemini put forth:.

At the end of my Christmas gift recommendation experiment, I had a hard time deciding which chatbot supplied me with the better selection of products.

In a recent development, both of them featured a strong selection of vinyl that I’m confident my dad would go crazy over after I revealed any of them as his gift. As for the gifts that were geared towards his music-based profession, both ChatGPT brought up one item while Gemini mentioned two recommendations. It was a close race, but I ended up siding with Gemini more during this latest AI tool faceoff. ChatGPT’s list is strong, no doubt. But Gemini’s clever inclusion of a custom rubber turntable slipmat with his favorite artist’s logo and custom-engraved hickory drumsticks stood out to me over ChatGPT’s inclusion of a record-washer kit.

Sources indicate that my dad is always in the market for upcoming drumsticks and I’m sure he’d do a backflip at the sight ot a turntable slipmat adorned with the iconic Prince symbol. Major kudos to Gemini for inching out ahead of ChatGPT’s gift recommendations and making my shopping a whole lot easier for him this holiday season (no gift cards this year!).

I implore everyone reading this to prompt both chatbots to give them equally memorable gift recommendations for the people they love based on their standout hobbies and interests.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Flang has matured, the developer tooling around it has lagged behind. In particular it lacks a dedicated debugger. LLDB lacks native Fortran support, it is only able to resolve basic breakpoints via raw line tables. This project adds support for Fortran in LLDB and lays the foundations on which a fully-featured Flang-backed debugger can be built.

Specifically, this work introduces native support for:.

In a recent development, because the upstreaming process for a project of this scale is ongoing, not all features have been merged into the LLVM main branch yet. However a working implementation is available for anyone to test. You can view the full set of changes, clone the code, and compile it yourself from my personal branch.

To keep up to date with the ongoing integration of this project, you can follow the tracking concern.

Adding a latest language to LLDB requires teaching it how to extract, represent, and display the values from compiled binaries. This relies on three core components:.

For more details on how to add a fresh language to LLDB, see the official documentation.

When proposing any significant change to LLVM, it first needs to go through the RFC process. In short, a proposal is written providing an overview of the change, the motivation behind it, the overall architecture of what will be changed, and open questions. It then receives feedback, and if consensus is reached, the change is accepted and can be upstreamed.

Reaching consensus on my RFC took approximately two months since it was a major newly introduced feature, but it taught me a lot about how to communicate an idea and interact with other developers.

The most important decisions we reached in the RFC were:.

For a large part of GSoC, development took place on my personal LLVM fork while waiting for community consensus on the RFC. Once consensus was reached, the focus shifted to breaking the work into small, incrementally testable pull requests that were easy for maintainers to review.

To ensure long-term stability without regressions, the implementation leverages LLDB’s lit-based testing infrastructure across two distinct levels:.

Unit Tests (C++): Added three test suites to test core components in isolation:.

API Tests (Python / SB API): End-to-end integration tests using LLDB’s Scripting Bridge API. These compile sample Fortran programs, launch debug sessions, and verify that the plugin, DWARF parser, and type system communicate properly to inspect variables and print output.

For more details on LLDB testing standards, see the official testing documentation.

It has been revealed that for API tests, LLDB needs to compile sample Fortran programs. This patch updated LLDB’s test runner to automatically detect an installed Fortran compiler and conditionally enable the Fortran test suite. PR #208298.

In a recent development, before adding actual language features, LLDB requires substantial boilerplate to satisfy its internal interfaces, specifically the TypeSystem, which demands numerous stub methods just to compile. To keep patches incremental and easy to review, this initial scaffolding was split into three minimal PRs that contain no active feature logic (except for registering the language plugin itself):.

Primitive types in Fortran consist of the INTEGER, REAL, LOGICAL and COMPLEX types and they are all described by the DW_TAG_base_type DWARF tag.

TypeSystemFortran manages the lifetime and representation of all Fortran types in LLDB:.

Add support for basic types in TypeSystemFortran PR #218269.

DWARFASTParserFortran bridges the raw debug symbols generated by the compiler and LLDB’s internal type system:.

To represent Fortran functions and subroutines, TypeSystemFortran tracks three key elements:.

When encountering a Fortran function or subroutine, DWARFASTParserFortran handles two main tasks:.

For variable values to be printed correctly, the TypeSystem provides information about how they should be displayed, such as their encoding and formatting, along with implementing DumpTypeValue to format and dump the value to a stream.

With this addition, frame variable can print variables in a predictable way:.

With this addition API tests were also added, since the output could not be tested before.

Recent findings suggest that pointers assosciated with non-array types are similar to C-like languages. So to handle them all that is needed is the pointee type.

Sources indicate that the TypeSystem creates a pointer type from the pointee type. It can also provide the pointee type from the pointer type and vice-versa.

The DW_TAG_pointer_type has a reference to the pointee type as a child, so the pointee type is recursively parsed using this reference and is forwarded to the TypeSystem.

Note on output: Variables appear with a mangled name because LLDB does not have access to the Flang demangler.

Arrays in Fortran can have custom bounds (e.g., indexing from -1 instead of 1) and custom byte strides (such as creating a slice consisting of every second element). In addition, Fortran arrays are column-major, unlike C/C++ which is row-major. For example, in a 2D array, elements of each column are stored in contiguous memory locations, whereas in C/C++ the elements of each row are contiguous. Furthermore, in Fortran, partial subscripting (such as indexing only one dimension of a multi-dimensional array) is invalid, unlike in C where it yields a pointer to a sub-array.

Below is a representation of how arrays are stored in the TypeSystem:.

Note: Star describes assumed-size arrays and colon describes allocatable arrays.

In a recent development, when executing frame variable for an array, LLDB resolves subscripts iteratively: it first resolves the base array, processes the first subscript, then resolves subsequent subscripts based on the previous result. Consequently, when a user queries arr[1] on a multi-dimensional array, LLDB should return a valid sub-array rather than an error. Because Fortran arrays are column-major, the elements of this sub-array are not contiguous in memory, but are instead separated by a byte stride. To handle this, a fresh sub-array type is created which strips the outermost dimension and scales the byte stride based on the extent and stride of the peeled dimension. This intermediate type is then returned, enabling LLDB to display the slice or continue stripping dimensions for chained subscripts.

The diagram below illustrates this resolution process:.

Industry observers note that assumed-size arrays use an asterisk (*) for their final dimension’s upper bound, leaving the total element count unknown in debug metadata. While handling follows the standard path, it differs in two ways:.

Unbounded Indexing: Upper-bound checks are bypassed, allowing direct element access (e.g., arr[10]) without failing on an unknown extent.

No Trailing Sub-Array Display: Because the final dimension lacks a known element count, LLDB cannot calculate child boundaries, meaning intermediate slices cannot list or display the sub-arrays that follow.

Note: While Fortran source syntax uses parentheses for multi-dimensional indexing (e.g., A(row, col)), LLDB’s frame variable expression path parser presently only supports chained C-style bracket notation (A[row][col]).

A DW_TAG_array_type tag is emitted in DWARF, with its children consisting of the element type as well as DW_TAG_subrange_type tags, one for each subrange, which can contain the following information:.

This information is collected and forwarded to TypeSystemFortran to create the array type.

Dynamic arrays in Fortran are described by an array descriptor, which holds information about the byte stride, lower/upper bounds, and each subrange’s element count. Because this information can change at runtime, it must be evaluated dynamically at the point of inspection.

Fortran compilers expose this metadata by emitting DWARF expressions, which evaluate the target memory state to calculate the runtime address and value of each attribute.

The primary architectural challenge was that LLDB as a whole assumes array geometry is static. Root structures like ValueObject and TypeSystem assume that while the values of array elements change at runtime, the structure of the array (such as its bounds and element count) does not, and if it does there is no way to know what that structure is. This model works for C, but breaks for Fortran, where the array’s true shape and element count can change during execution and the debugger can know what the array’s structure is.

According to recent reports, rather than making intrusive changes to core LLDB interfaces, a provider for synthetic children was used. Its job is to read the runtime descriptor in target memory and instantiate a newly introduced, concrete type containing the active bounds and strides. This cleanly accommodates Fortran’s dynamic layouts while keeping the TypeSystem isolated from runtime state.

Industry observers note that for arrays whose properties depend on runtime variables (such as bounds determined by function arguments), compilers emit a hidden variable in the DWARF metadata containing the required values. Because this information resides in runtime memory, it is resolved by the synthetic children provider using the same mechanism as array descriptors.

These arrays appear in functions, allowing callers to pass arrays of varying dimensions to the same routine. For these arrays, the compiler emits a single DW_TAG_generic_subrange instead of one subrange tag per dimension, along with a rank attribute (DW_AT_rank) that provides the actual rank. Using the DWARF expressions found in the generic subrange’s children, the runtime properties of each dimension are determined. This resolution is handled by the synthetic children provider.

The required DWARF expressions are stored directly within the array type, ensuring the TypeSystem does not process arrays containing runtime information. During frame variable evaluation, LLDB first attempts to retrieve a child from the TypeSystem. If the static type cannot provide one, the request falls back to the synthetic children provider. The provider resolves the runtime metadata into a concrete type and passes that resolved type back to the TypeSystem for standard processing.

Industry observers note that the DWARF information for arrays can either be a DWARF expression, a reference to a variable or a number. The DWARFASTParser has to figure out what type of array it is and activate the appropriate flags. Its job is to inform the TypeSystem what to expect and forward all information.

Recent findings suggest that fortran is a case insensitive language and LLDB did not have support for performing case-insensitive lookups. Compilers emit a DW_AT_identifier_case attribute which gives information regarding the casing. Using this attribute LLDB sets the correct appropriate casing. For mixed-language executables, where one language is case-insensitive and the other isn’t, LLDB defaults to being case-sensitive.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, arrays proved to be a lot more complex and time-consuming than we originally anticipated, so the scope of the project changed. The following features will be implemented in the future:.

As discussed in the RFC, the ideal end-point of this project is to have an expression evaluator using Flang, rather than relying only on the frame variable command (which uses a language-agnostic parser called DIL).

According to recent reports, this was my first professional project and also my first time collaborating with many people. The hardest thing for me was learning how to communicate effectively and finding my voice in a large community. Thankfully, my mentors helped me a lot with this, enabling me to become much more confident in group discussions.

Sources indicate that I learned a lot about navigating a large codebase. By the end of the project, I was completing tasks much faster and finding information more easily. Just as importantly, I realized how vital clear communication is in a major project, and how much difference a supportive, helpful community can make.

I want to say a substantial thank you to my mentors, Shivam Gupta and Tarun Prabhu. They were immensely helpful throughout this project and taught me a lot. I also want to thank the LLVM community—especially the LLDB team—for taking the time to give me feedback on the RFC for this project and helping me along the way.

Janelle James is a Grand Theft Auto fan celebrating being part of GTA VI as consumers worldwide get their hands on the long-awaited game.

In a new social media post, the Abbott Elementary star explained how she got involved in the game.

“It’s very key to me that everybody knows that not only is that me, I’m not simply ‘voice acting,'” James shared on her Instagram Stories. “I pursued, conceptualized, pitched, scripted AND voice acted my radio show.”.

She continued, “Rockstar [Games] didn’t ‘choose’ me, I bullied my way to them. I’ve been playing this game since Vice City (was previously overcommitted to Metal Gear), and this is a literal dream come true!!”.

The stand-up comedian said that she’s been “told the response is already great,” adding, “Hope to catch yall in these online streets where I will promptly kick you square in your back then put 2 in your dome.” Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that as players explore the GTA VI world, some noticed a very familiar voice in the game. James appears in the game as the host of She Got Assets. Players have been clipping the moment, which you can preview in the video below.

Industry observers note that janelle James from Abbott Elementary?!?!?! #GTA6 pic.twitter.com/LKErMij010.

Grand Theft Auto VI is an action-adventure game developed by Rockstar Games and is the eighth main entry in the GTA video game series. The long-awaited game comes 16 years after 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V. Set in the fictional Vice City (based on Miami), the new game is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for the most affordable option, the Vibe One projector is just $179 (originally $299) after a 40% discount. It already comes with Google TV, which is my favorite OS, so you can download and stream any app you want. It's battery-powered, which means you can take it anywhere with you (as long as you have wifi). You also have the option of getting the bundle with the PowerBase Stand, which extends the battery to five hours. The battery life, OS system, stand, speakers, and auto keystone technology are the same—but the bundles are different, so they're worth considering if they fit your needs.

It supports 4K resolution, uses RGB triple laser brightness that reaches 4800 ISO lumens (bright enough to see during the day), has a 120Hz refresh rate and gaming features to make gaming smooth, displays an 8,000:1 native contrast to make colors and blacks pop, and supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision, and HDR10+. Right now, it's down to $1,899 (originally $2,499) after a 24% discount.

#51026. Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (848 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

In a recent development, if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an glitch with the Duo itself.

Industry observers note that I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

According to recent reports, I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for shows and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Industry observers note that multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

It has been revealed that after a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

It has been revealed that I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

In a recent development, I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Recent findings suggest that is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

Industry observers note that the iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique newly introduced iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

Sources indicate that what has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods users thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

It has been revealed that with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

Industry observers note that airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

It has been revealed that you can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Industry observers note that apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

Sources indicate that in iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods people, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the latest Siri. It will let consumers do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

Earlier this year when AirTag 2 released, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

It has been revealed that now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.
