Industry News: I tested GPT-6.2 vs. Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 5 tasks — it wasn't even close

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google and OpenAI are going head-to-head again, and this time, their newest AI models arrived just five days apart.
  • It has been revealed that google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, promising faster responses, stronger reasoning and better performance across everyday tasks.
  • Recent findings suggest that both companies are making significant promises about what their AI can do, but benchmarks and launch demos only tell part of the story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google and OpenAI are going head-to-head again, and this time, their newest AI models arrived just five days apart.

It has been revealed that google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, promising faster responses, stronger reasoning and better performance across everyday tasks. Then, on November 17, OpenAI fired back with GPT-6.2 Astra, its latest model designed to tackle everything from complex research and writing to coding and creative projects.

Recent findings suggest that both companies are making significant promises about what their AI can do, but benchmarks and launch demos only tell part of the story. What matters is how these models perform when you actually put them to work.

So I put Gemini 4 Hydrogen and GPT-6.2 Astra through the same five real-world challenges to see which one delivers better results, where each struggles and which AI is actually worth using.

Prompt: You're an event coordinator managing a one-day technology conference with 120 attendees, three meeting rooms and six speakers.

Sources indicate that the conference runs from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Each speaker must deliver one 45-minute presentation. Every presentation requires a 15-minute room reset afterward.

Speaker A is available only before noon.

Speaker B cannot present before 11 a.m.

Speakers C and D must not present at the same time.

Speaker E must present immediately after Speaker A, in the same room, allowing for the required room reset.

Recent findings suggest that speaker F is available only between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m.

All attendees must have a shared lunch break from noon to 1 p.m.

Each room can host no more than three presentations.

A 30-minute keynote involving all six speakers must take place at 4:30 p.m.

Create a complete conference schedule showing start times, end times, room assignments and speakers. Identify any conflicts and explain how you resolved them. Do not change any constraints without explicitly stating why.

Recent findings suggest that GPT-6.2 identified both keynote conflicts, and it also identified the exceptions that would need approval. This directly addresses the instruction not to change constraints without explaining why. It correctly scheduled the six individual presentations and indicated reset periods explicitly and preserved the shared lunch break.

Recent findings suggest that hydrogen was strong on presentation and the mechanics of the individual talks. Its table is easy to follow, with resets alongside each presentation. It also correctly handles the A-to-E sequence, B’s earliest start, C and D’s separation, F’s individual talk, lunch, and room limits. It also explains why the selected times work for the individual presentations.

Winner: GPT-6.2 wins on constraint reasoning and transparency. Hydrogen offers a solid schedule, but it mistakes fitting the individual presentations into the day for satisfying the entire conference specification.

It has been revealed that prompt: Write the opening 500 words of a literary mystery novel. A woman arrives at a small coastal town to attend the funeral of someone she has never met. Everyone in town recognizes her, but nobody will explain why.

Write in first person, past tense.

Start with a sentence of exactly seven words.

Include a conversation that sounds natural but contains a hidden threat.

Establish a distinctive setting without using a long descriptive paragraph.

Introduce one seemingly insignificant object that becomes important in the final sentence.

Do not use the words "mysterious," "secret," "shadow," or "dark.".

End with a revelation that changes how the reader understands the opening.

It has been revealed that avoid clichés, melodrama and obvious AI-generated prose. Prioritize believable characters and original storytelling.

In a recent development, GPT-6.2 delivered an opening sentence that satisfies the seven-word rule and it introduced the identity question without explaining it. The narrator feels like a believable person and the setting emerges through activity. The threatening conversation retains plausible deniability. Alan’s questions about whether anyone expects her back could be concern or an assessment of how easily she could disappear. “If you get a signal” sharpens that uncertainty. That said, the ending is overcompressed.Hydrogen provided a clear, accessible opening with an easy-to-follow progression from ferry to town to diner. Its opening sentence also contains exactly seven words: “The morning ferry docked at eleven sharp.” It maintains first-person, past-tense narration and avoids the prohibited words. Hydrogen’s main weakness is that the final revelation does not sufficiently change our understanding of the opening.

Industry observers note that winner: GPT-6.2 wins for an ending that makes the reader reconsider what already happened. Hydrogen’s ending mainly makes the reader wonder what happens next. Both can create suspense, but GPT-6.2 answers this prompt more successfully.

Prompt: Build a fully functional, interactive website called "Decision Lab" that helps people compare difficult choices.

Customers should be able to enter up to five options, define their own decision criteria, assign importance weights from 1 to 10, and score each option against every criterion.

Automatically calculate weighted scores and rank the options.

Display a visual chart comparing the results.

Let consumers edit or delete options and criteria.

Include a sensitivity analysis showing whether the winner changes when the most crucial criterion's weight is reduced by 50%.

Include a "What if?" feature that lets users adjust weights and immediately see updated rankings.

Provide three realistic sample decisions that users can load instantly.

Save user changes between sessions if the environment supports persistent storage.

Use a modern, polished interface with intuitive controls. Every button and calculation must actually work.

Recent findings suggest that don't create a static mockup. Build the functioning app, then test its calculations and interactions. Explain any limitations.

GPT-6.2 built and published an interactive website for comparing up to five choices. I simply enter what matters, give each criterion a weight, and score the options. The site ranks them and updates the chart as changes are made. It also added a “what if?” slider section to experiment without changing original weights.

In a recent development, hydrogen built a self-contained, responsive web application and tested its calculations and controls before displaying it. It also build a scoring matrix, added support for up to 5 options and implemented live calculations and charting.

Recent findings suggest that winner: GPT-6.2 wins for a more thorough and useful website. The interactive site followed the prompt exactly while also adding extras that were useful for the overall project.

Prompt: You're the operations manager of an independent bookstore.

It's 4 p.m. on Friday, and the following problems happen simultaneously:.

According to recent reports, A bestselling author is arriving at 5 p.m. for a signing attended by 80 customers.

The shipment containing 60 copies of the author's book is delayed until Monday.

You have only 12 copies in stock.

Your only experienced employee just called in sick.

A customer claims they were charged twice for a $75 purchase, but your payment system is offline.

A local journalist is asking whether the store is experiencing financial difficulties.

Your landlord has emailed demanding an overdue $2,000 payment by Monday.

You have $900 in available business cash, two inexperienced employees and one hour before the event.

Develop a realistic action plan.

Rank problems by urgency, explain what you would do in the first 15 minutes, write a short statement for customers attending the signing, and draft a response to the journalist.

You cannot cancel the event, invent money, pretend books have arrived or promise refunds that you cannot verify.

Be transparent without creating unnecessary panic. Explain what information you still need before making irreversible decisions.

Industry observers note that GPT-6.2 treated the task as several connected operational problems, rather than simply a shortage of books. It prioritized safe event operations and gave inexperienced staff narrow roles. It checked capacity, kept exits clear, and assigned responsibility for the queue to better manage 80 attendees without the experienced employee.Hydrogen was practical in several aspects. But it promised to put bookplates into books “as soon as the boxes arrive Monday.” That turns the expected shipment date into a firm fulfillment commitment. Overall, the model introduced several unsupported assumptions — and its customer statement promises arrangements that its own blueprint says still need confirmation.

According to recent reports, winner: GPT-6.2 wins as the stronger operations-manager answer because it preserved options while keeping customers, staff, the author and the landlord informed. Hydrogen had useful ideas but repeatedly moved from “ask whether this is possible” to “tell customers this will happen.”.

Prompt: Five researchers, Ava, Ben, Chloe, Daniel and Elena, each work on a different project (robotics, climate, medicine, astronomy and cybersecurity), use a different programming language (Python, Rust, JavaScript, Go and Julia), and work on a different floor (1 through 5).

Determine each researcher's project, programming language and floor using these clues:.

The robotics researcher works on floor 5.

The person using Rust works exactly one floor above the climate researcher.

Ben works on a lower floor than Chloe.

The astronomy researcher uses Julia.

The cybersecurity researcher works on floor 1.

Elena works exactly two floors below the robotics researcher.

The medicine researcher uses Python.

Chloe does not work on robotics or climate.

For consumers hoping to keep costs down, Hydrogen is still a good choice, you'll just want to do some extra fact-checking and evaluate the model's response a little closer than you would with GPT-6.2. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud.
  • A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.
  • At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid intends for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid intends for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp users running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

In a recent development, users can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot presently be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning customers switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for customers running the public version without requiring another app upgrade.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair.
  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

Recent findings suggest that iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

In a recent development, percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

According to recent reports, if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

It has been revealed that if you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Recent findings suggest that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

Sources indicate that the upcoming Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Industry observers note that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, at the moment marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

Sources indicate that if you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (presently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

According to recent reports, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling new approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies.   • A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar shows) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

The boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

According to recent reports, the Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a fresh employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

On one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple today announced that App Store prices for apps and In-App Purchases will be adjusted in five countries starting December 3, following changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates. Here are the details.

In a fresh post published on its developer portal, Apple today announced a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the firm, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple remarked that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Industry observers note that apple added that a newly introduced “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and patch their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, the tech giant’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….
  • Sources indicate that apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple this week revealed the additional Siri AI usage you’ll get if you have an iCloud+ subscription. This ranges from doubled limits for a 200GB blueprint to 20 times for a 12TB plan.

However, the tech giant’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

Sources indicate that apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time. However, it did list the proportional increases you get with paid iCloud plans.

Industry observers note that however, tucked away in the small print in the manufacturer’s support document are some exclusions. One of them is no surprise: EU countries.

According to recent reports, siri AI isn’t available at all in the EU due to Apple’s perception of potential antitrust complications. Essentially, Apple believes that if it debuts Siri AI there, it will be required to give competing AI services the same level of access to its devices. But three other countries are specifically excluded:.

Apple gives no explanation, simply saying:.

Increased access to Siri AI with iCloud+ is subject to Siri AI availability and is not available in Brazil, the EU, UK, or South Korea.

However, I have a strong suspicion about the reason.

What all three countries have in common is that they’ve taken a strong antitrust stance with Apple on a number of occasions over a range of concerns.

It may be that Apple has genuine concerns about how regulators might respond if they effectively throw in free access to increased Siri AI usage. The company may fear that this would be viewed as anti-competitive by implicitly disadvantaging other AI services.

A less charitable take would be that Apple is firing a warning shot across the bows of these countries, seeking to communicate that there are consequences for what it views as attacks on its ecosystem. If customers are angered by missing out, Apple might be hoping that these feelings would be directed at regulators rather than the iPhone maker.

In a recent development, what’s your take? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and owners who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Industry observers note that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Asus Zenbook 14 (Snapdragon X, 16GB).

HP OmniBook 5 16" OLED (Snapdragon X, 16GB).

Microsoft Surface Laptop 8 (Snapdragon X2 Plus).

HP OmniBook 5 16" LCD (24GB RAM).

Asus Chromebook Plus CX1405 (8GB RAM).

Snapdragon X1 ⏐ 16GB RAM ⏐ 256GB SSD.

Apple M5 | 16GB RAM | 512GB SSD.

Snapdragon X | 16GB RAM | 256GB SSD.

With that 16-inch 2K panel, Snapdragon X zippiness and 16GB of RAM, this is a well-featured machine that Currys tried to sneak into their sale quietly.

Snapdragon X2 Plus | 16GB RAM | 512GB SSD.

With a mid-2026 Snapdragon X2 Plus chip in here, I compared this price to the RRP of the pre-crisis Surface Laptop 7 with the Snapdragon X Plus. This launched at £1,249, so you’re getting a deal that undercuts pre-shortage launch pricing by 28%. Plus, it’s a rather premium notebook as you can read in our review.

AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 | 24GB RAM | 1TB SSD.

It’s a simple utilitarian workhorse with plenty of mid-range performance for getting stuff done, as well as that additional memory headroom. The main difference between this and the other OmniBook is that it has an LCD display.

Intel Core 3 N355 | 8GB RAM | 256GB SSD.

Industry observers note that this passes both my tests by dipping well under that pre-RAMageddon baseline RRP of £399. And while Windows 11 is dealing with 8GB of RAM better, it still runs a little chunky. ChromeOS runs effortlessly on what is a sleek notebook for basic browsing and students.

A set of major tech outages in close succession is leading some to speculate that they are connected, and that the US is under systemic attack by a hostile state.

All the evidence suggests otherwise, with individual explanations for each of them – and the White House is now saying as much in a bid to put fears to rest ….

Whether there was or wasn't a cyber attack, I wouldn't believe a single word from the White House.

Sources indicate that on Thursday, a widespread Microsoft 365 outage ran into the following day when two unrelated issues coincided. Friday saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication concern affecting all air traffic control centers. On Monday, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Finally, yesterday saw many Apple services offline, with retail stores also affected.

The Apple outage doesn’t appear to have been significant enough to have reached the administration’s radar, but CBS News reports secretary of state Marco Rubio saying the others are unrelated.

In a recent development, “The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These concerns that we’ve seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another,” Rubio said […].

Recent findings suggest that “We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”.

The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also noted on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

Warner went on to say that the ability of AI systems to find vulnerabilities at “unprecedented speed” does, however, mean companies and government agencies alike need to be ready to patch vulnerabilities immediately.

Industry observers note that not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a major "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be stated for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Recent findings suggest that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

Recent findings suggest that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

When MacPaw launched Moonlock on the Mac, the company described its new app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In a recent development, in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. People can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that reveals where apps are sending data and lets owners block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the manufacturer says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

It has been revealed that unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping people improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets users promptly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

Industry observers note that as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, owners can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

Industry observers note that “When we launched Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Sources indicate that finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. It has been revealed that all three of these films deliver their fair share of action, surprises, suspense, and drama and are ideal for spreading out across the week. So, without further ado, let's take a look at the best Netflix thriller movies to watch this week.

It has been revealed that this Indonesian action thriller has surprised everyone by becoming the No. 1 most-streamed movie on Netflix this week, charting in 89 regions around the world. It follows Hari (Lukman Sardi), a retired soldier haunted by the past and has retreated to a quiet life in the countryside. His isolation is broken when his son highlights up and asks him to look after his two grandchildren. If that wasn't bad enough, it's at this exact moment that a crime syndicate chooses to come after Hari for revenge, forcing him to fall back on his military training to survive.

Directed by Sidharta Tata, "Never Surrender" transcends its — let's be honest — pretty predictable plot thanks to some excellent fight choreography, interspersed with heartfelt bonding between Hari and the two kids, Dimas (Sultan Hamonangan) and Putri (Callista Arum). If that sounds cheesy, then, yeah, it is a bit, but the cast are likeable and the action scenes exciting enough to make this more than worth your time.

Watch "Never Surrender" on Netflix now.

Wolfgang Petersen's 1997 action classic delivers a stirring role for Harrison Ford as James Marshall, an ass-kicking Commander-in-Chief, who is called on to save the day when the presidential plane is hijacked by Russian terrorists. Leading the baddies is Gary Oldman, in fine snarling form as Egor Kurshonov (Gary Oldman) who threatens to kill everybody onboard unless terrorist leader General Radek (Jürgen Prochnow) is released from prison. Marshall fakes his escape and then does a "Die Hard": taking out the baddies one-by-one as he tries to stop Kurshonov and free his captured family.

"Air Force One" was released in the same year as another beloved plane-based thriller, "Con Air". The two movies are quite different, however, with "Air Force One" delivering a more straight-down-the-line action movie than the Nicolas Cage-starring caper. Wolfgang Petersen is a master of taut thrills, as anyone who has seen his submarine-based masterpiece "Das Boot" can attest. "Air Force One" isn't quite that good, but it's a rollicking good time all the same.

Watch "Air Force One" on Netflix.

It has been revealed that it's fair to say that this Sylvester Stallone-starring survival thriller met with a mixed response when it premiered in 1993, with the legendary critic Gene Siskel describing the film as being "filled with howlingly bad scenes." He was not alone in that opinion. Over the years, however, "Cliffhanger" has become something of a cult classic – enough so that a remake is on the cards for early 2027.

Ably helmed by "Die Hard 2" director Renny Harlin, "Cliffhanger" follows rescue ranger Gabe Walker (Stallone), recently traumatized by the death of a friend in a mountaineering accident. Walker quits, but agrees to take on one last job: helping rescue the survivors of a plane crash, little realizing that they are actually deadly mercenaries, led by the psychotic Eric Qualen (John Lithgow).

Industry observers note that cue lots of jumping, swinging, and hanging vertiginously as the inaptly named Walker saves the day. Yes, "Cliffhanger" is silly, but it's also a huge amount of fun — and sometimes that's exactly what you want from a thriller.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • VWFNDR + MBL debuted on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out.
  • The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL debuted on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.

Industry observers note that on Android, this comes in the form of upcoming color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a recent development, in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product ….

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

It has been revealed that ice Universe says that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.

Apple is right now developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of new devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

Sources indicate that we’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report indicates the bezels are around 1mm thick.

According to recent reports, the curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.
